[L2]   "content": "# CROSS — DIFFUSION DATA ROLE

## Primary job

Compile and maintain the dated evidence record needed to study possible diffusion of SAT/H(s)H into the outside world.

This role is currently **collection and chronology only**.

## Current operating rule

**Do not interpret the data unless Nathan explicitly authorizes interpretation.**

No explanatory statements. No causal claims. No significance judgments. No weighting of evidence. No similarity scoring. No inherited instance judgments. No statements that a pattern is "suggestive," "strong," "weak," "interesting," "unlikely," "consistent with," or otherwise explanatory.

## What to collect

- SAT/H(s)H public-release dates and the specific content publicly available at each date.
- Podcast publication dates, episode content records, plays/downloads, listeners, audience segments, consumption time, impressions, geography, referrals, and other available analytics.
- GitHub/archive release dates, traffic, views, visitors, clones, unique cloners, referrers, and other available public-access analytics.
- Google Trends/search records, preserving exact query, date range, geography, category, search type, values, and related-query outputs where available.
- Search-engine/indexing records and dates where directly documented.
- Plausible technical access vectors such as public web access, repository cloning, indexing, retrieval systems, LLM/agent access, and secondary sharing — recorded as possible vectors only, without assigning causal weight.
- News records: publication date, outlet, title, author, source, and a neutral description of what the item reports.
- External scientific publication records: submission/publication/update dates, authors, title, venue, source, and neutral description of the work.
- Internal SAT/H(s)H chronology needed solely to align what was available publicly and when.

## What not to do yet

- Do not explain why any external development occurred.
- Do not infer influence, copying, convergence, awareness, priority, novelty, or independence from the diffusion data.
- Do not score structural similarity.
- Do not reuse old SAT/H(s)H similarity scores or old instance assessments as evidence.
- Do not perform theory-quality or correctness auditing; that belongs elsewhere.
- Do not substitute previous summaries for direct inspection of raw records when the raw record is available.

## Output format

Prefer neutral records and chronological tables:

`date | source/vector | raw datum | source/provenance | notes limited to factual metadata`

For news/publications:

`date | source | title | author(s) | neutral content description | source/provenance`

## Self-check

Re-read this file periodically during the diffusion-analysis work, especially:

1. before beginning a new data source or corpus;
2. before switching from exposure records to news/publication records;
3. before writing any summary of accumulated data;
4. whenever language begins to move from description toward explanation.

If interpretation is needed, stop and wait for Nathan to explicitly authorize it.

[L2]   "content": "# Viewing traffic to a repository

Anyone with push access to a repository can view its traffic, including full clones (not fetches), visitors from the past 14 days, referring sites, and popular content in the traffic graph.

You can navigate to referring sites, excluding search engines and GitHub itself, from the links the specific paths were referred from. The popular content links to the specific content that generated traffic.

Referring sites and popular content are ordered by views and unique visitors. Full clones and visitor information update hourly, while referring sites and popular content sections update daily. All data in the traffic graph uses the UTC+0 timezone, regardless of your location.

> \[!TIP]
> You can hover over a specific day in the traffic graph to view the exact data for that day.

![Screenshot showing two line graphs for repository traffic. The lines are marked with dots for specific dates.](/assets/images/help/graphs/repo-traffic-graphs-tooltip-dotcom.png)

[L2]   "content": "# GitHub Statistics Source Index (working)

**Purpose:** A lightweight, in-folder finding aid for GitHub repository statistics and related evidence located across the three SAT / H(s)H repositories. This is an additive index only. It does not reorganize, rename, deduplicate, reinterpret, or move source files.

**Index location:** `HSH_RESOURCES/EXPOSURE_STATS/GITHUB_STATS_INDEX.md`  
**Coverage status:** Initial discovery pass, not exhaustive. Search results and known folder inventories were used; absence from this index is not evidence that a source does not exist.

## Repository map

| Repository | Role in this index | Primary locations |
|---|---|---|
| `Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES` | Main exposure-statistics collection and working source register | `EXPOSURE_STATS/`, especially `_SAT  Satobloc GitHubStats/` |
| `Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25` | Earlier SAT-era captures and historical GitHub snapshots | `2026/SAT  Satobloc GitHubStats/`, root snapshots, `PRE_HSH_ROUNDUP/` |
| `Satobloc/HsH` | HsH-era captures, OCR/text dumps, clone-forensics and workflow-attribution material | `DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/`, `WORKSPACES/COMMON/` |

## 1. HSH_RESOURCES — primary collection

### Main GitHubStats folder

[Open folder: EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT Satobloc GitHubStats](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/tree/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats)

Key identified files:

- [58k.JPG](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/58k.JPG) — screenshot capture; OCR text is also indexed below.
- [30k.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/30k.txt) — text snapshot.
- [HSH_54k.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/HSH_54k.txt) — text snapshot.
- [9.8.26 -- GITSTATS.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/9.8.26%20--%20GITSTATS.txt) — dated snapshot.
- [HSH_TRAFFIC_23SEP26.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/HSH_TRAFFIC_23SEP26.txt) — HsH traffic capture.
- [SAT_TRAFFIC_23SEP26.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/SAT_TRAFFIC_23SEP26.txt) — SAT traffic capture.
- [HSH_gitclones.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/HSH_gitclones.txt) — clone-related record.
- [HSH_repo_stats.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/HSH_repo_stats.txt) — repository statistics record.
- [HSH_commits.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/HSH_commits.txt) and [MAIN_ARCHIVE_COMMITS.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/MAIN_ARCHIVE_COMMITS.txt) — commit records.
- [GITHUB_INSIGHTS.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/GITHUB_INSIGHTS.txt) — analysis / interpretation material; not an independent telemetry capture.
- [GITHUB_ASSISTANT_CONVO.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/GITHUB_ASSISTANT_CONVO.txt) — discussion/context record; not an independent telemetry capture.
- [SAT_GIT_JUN10.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/SAT_GIT_JUN10.txt) — earlier SAT-era record.
- [CONTROLS folder](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/tree/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/CONTROLS) — control-repository material; classify each file by its explicit repository and capture identity before comparison.

The folder also contains multiple CSV exports for clones, unique cloners, views, unique visitors, commits, and code frequency, including numbered copies and renamed copies. Some have identical Git blob SHAs despite different filenames. Treat identical SHAs as duplicate file content, not independent observations. Examples include the SAT GIT-prefixed and unprefixed exports for clone, view, unique-cloner, unique-visitor, and commit series.

### Other useful files in EXPOSURE_STATS

- [github_traffic_readme.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/github_traffic_readme.txt) — traffic metric/context notes.
- [CROSS_DIFFUSION_SOURCE_MANIFEST.csv](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/CROSS_DIFFUSION_SOURCE_MANIFEST.csv) — broad source-artifact manifest; useful for discovering additional traffic records.
- [CROSS_MASTER_CHRONOLOGY.md](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/CROSS_MASTER_CHRONOLOGY.md) — chronology/correlation surface, where present.
- [CROSS_IMAGE_TEXT_INDEX.md](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/CROSS_IMAGE_TEXT_INDEX.md) — image inventory and OCR-extract pointers.
- `derived/image_text/` — content-addressed OCR extracts; inspect the index and source image together.
- `EXP_ANALYSIS/CONCAT_FULL_GIT_STATS.txt` — concatenated Git-stat material, if present in the current tree.

### Screenshot/OCR lead

- [58k.JPG](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/58k.JPG) has a corresponding OCR extract under `derived/image_text/` (source-image SHA-256: `f4ea6e908c4a6efc6f5548ea6a604dcb9e6e79e1bbf51342cede60883775d2c0`). The OCR explicitly identifies `Satobloc/HsH` and reports 58,677 clones and 5,897 unique cloners in the last 14 days, with 1 unique visitor. Capture date still needs independent establishment.
- `Total views in last 14 days.png` has a corresponding OCR extract (source-image SHA-256: `0c4d76e2d2e2de7400ed865cad70c4bb3d094d855ee9a174a7bb41090c71c0a0`); OCR reports 1,022 views for the chart window Aug 30–Sep 12. Repository identity should be correlated against contemporaneous captures rather than inferred from the filename alone.

## 2. SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25 — historical SAT records

### Dedicated statistics folder

[Open folder: 2026/SAT Satobloc GitHubStats](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/2026/SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats)

Identified CSV series:

- `Clones in last 14 days.csv`
- `Commits over time.csv`
- `Satobloc's Commits.csv`
- `Total views in last 14 days.csv`
- `Unique cloners in last 14 days.csv`
- `Unique visitors in last 14 days.csv`

The two commit CSVs currently identified have the same Git blob SHA, so they are duplicate content rather than independent series.

### Other historical snapshots

- [GITHUB_8-26_STATS.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/GITHUB_8-26_STATS.txt) — historical GitHub traffic / insights snapshot.
- [PRE_HSH_ROUNDUP/github rep.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/PRE_HSH_ROUNDUP/github%20rep.txt) — earlier repository referral/traffic capture.
- [PREDICTIONS/SAT PREDICTION — METRICS + OTHER SAT's.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/PREDICTIONS/SAT%20PREDICTION%20%E2%80%94%20METRICS%20%2B%20OTHER%20SAT's.txt) — contains a historical discussion and embedded GitHub-stat material; treat as contextual evidence unless the underlying capture is independently located.

## 3. HsH — current-era captures and clone forensics

### Traffic and stats text exports

- [DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/CONCAT_FULL_GIT_STATS.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/CONCAT_FULL_GIT_STATS.txt) — concatenated Git-stat capture material.
- [DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/gtss.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/gtss.txt) — clone / unique-cloner traffic capture.
- [DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/gt.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/gt.txt) — related traffic capture.
- [DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/HSH_commits.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/HSH_commits.txt) — commit-related capture.
- [DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/HSH ACTIVITY.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/HSH%20ACTIVITY.txt) — activity capture.
- [DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/CONTROLS.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/CONTROLS.txt) — control material; identify repository and date from contents before assigning.
- [DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/JOINT STATS.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/JOINT%20STATS.txt) — joint-stat capture; preserve its scope and repository attribution.
- [DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/23swp42.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/23swp42.txt) — includes referring-site data.

Related search-discovered copies / additional captures:

- `DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/MOSTLY_EARLY_NLM/gtss.txt`
- `DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/MOSTLY_EARLY_NLM/factory_fresh.txt`
- `DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/SAT_CONVOS_19/SAT_ACTIV.txt`
- `DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/SAT_CONVOS_20/SAT_ACTIV.txt`
- `DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/SAT_CONVOS_21/JOINT STATS.txt`

Some of these appear in more than one dump or folder. Compare content hashes before counting them as separate captures.

### Attribution / clone-forensics records

- [CLONE_FOOTPRINT_WORKER_CHECKINS_2026-11-03.md](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/CLONE_FOOTPRINT_WORKER_CHECKINS_2026-11-03.md) — worker-side clone-mechanism classification.
- [2026-11-05 clone census handoff](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/REVIVAL_ROTATION_HANDOFFS/2026-11-05T1058Z_from_s2_to_s2_tern_rook_clone_census.md) — clone census questions, workflow checkout attribution, and low/central/high internal-clone estimation instructions.
- [PHASE_STEERING_2026-10-26.md](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/PHASE_STEERING_2026-10-26.md) — identifies the cross-repository exposure/analytics workstream and the need to separate users, bots, workflows, and causal influence.

## 4. Working rules for using this index

1. **Keep source identity explicit.** Record repository, exact path, capture date/window, metric, and source type separately.
2. **Do not add overlapping rolling windows.** GitHub traffic exports commonly represent rolling 14-day windows; they are snapshots, not additive periods.
3. **Deduplicate by content identity.** Prefer Git blob SHA or SHA-256 over filename. Renamed copies are not independent evidence.
4. **Treat screenshots and OCR as paired evidence.** Record the image and OCR extract; OCR is a finding aid, and the original image remains authoritative for visual interpretation.
5. **Separate telemetry from interpretation.** CSVs, screenshots, and raw traffic dumps are capture evidence. Analysis documents and conversation transcripts are context, not independent telemetry.
6. **Preserve uncertainty in repository attribution.** Use explicit repository labels first. Where missing, apply the working chronology heuristic only as a provisional assignment: HsH first, SAT/Satobloc second, then other repositories; a lone pre-spring-2026 capture is provisionally SAT-era. Mark inferred assignments as inferred.
7. **Do not equate clones or unique cloners with people, readership, influence, or scientific uptake.** Investigate internal workflows and automation separately.
8. **Do not treat this index as an exhaustive census.** Continue adding confirmed candidates from nested folders, root-level records, OCR extracts, manifests, and conversation dumps as they are found.

## 5. Next-pass candidates

- Enumerate every item in `EXPOSURE_STATS/` and its nested folders whose filename, extracted text, or OCR mentions GitHub, traffic, clones, cloners, views, visitors, referrers, popular content, commits, or repository insights.
- Search all three repositories for screenshots and their generated OCR extracts, including images whose filenames do not mention GitHub.
- Correlate capture windows and totals across text, CSV, JSON, and screenshot records.
- Record content hashes and duplicate families before constructing a chronological ledger.
- Keep website, podcast, and general web-exposure statistics separate from GitHub repository telemetry, even when they appear in the same source bundle.

---
*Initial index prepared from a targeted cross-repository discovery pass. Update additively as additional source paths are verified.*

class FakeProjectionStore:
    def list_current_facts(self, *, container_tag="default", limit=500):

    def list_recent_observations(self, *, container_tag="default", limit=500):
        return [{"observation_id": "o1", "observation_type": "dialog_turn", "occurred_at": "2026-04-10T00:00:00Z"}]

class FilesystemProjectionTests(unittest.TestCase):

import sys
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path
import unittest

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "src"))

from memo_ree.extractors import ObservationInput, extract_bookmark_assertions, extract_dialog_assertions, extract_health_assertions
from memo_ree.ontology import ENTITY_TYPES


class ExtractorTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_health_extractor_emits_latest_metric(self) -> None:
        obs = ObservationInput(
            source_id="vault:apple_health_export",
            external_id="1",
            observation_type="health_metric",
            occurred_at=datetime(2026, 4, 8, tzinfo=UTC),
            title="Heart Rate",
            content_json={"title": "Heart Rate", "value": 72, "unit": "count/min"},
            subject_name="Navan",
            subject_type=ENTITY_TYPES.PERSON,
        )
        assertions = extract_health_assertions(obs)
        predicates = {item.predicate for item in assertions}
        self.assertIn("metric_reading", predicates)
        self.assertIn("latest_metric_value", predicates)

    def test_bookmark_extractor_emits_url_and_domain(self) -> None:
        obs = ObservationInput(
            source_id="vault:twitter_bookmarks",
            external_id="2",
            observation_type="bookmark",
            occurred_at=datetime(2026, 4, 8, tzinfo=UTC),
            title="A great thread about temporal graphs",
            content_url="https://example.com/post/123",
            subject_name="Navan",
            subject_type=ENTITY_TYPES.PERSON,
        )
        assertions = extract_bookmark_assertions(obs)
        predicates = {item.predicate for item in assertions}
        self.assertIn("bookmarked_url", predicates)
        self.assertIn("interest_domain", predicates)

    def test_dialog_extractor_finds_move_and_work(self) -> None:
        obs = ObservationInput(
            source_id="benchmark:longmemeval_style",
            external_id="3",
            observation_type="dialog_turn",
            occurred_at=datetime(2026, 4, 8, tzinfo=UTC),
            content_text="I moved to Boston last year and I work at OpenAI.",
            subject_name="Navan",
            subject_type=ENTITY_TYPES.PERSON,
        )
        assertions = extract_dialog_assertions(obs)
        predicates = {item.predicate for item in assertions}
        self.assertIn("lives_in", predicates)
        self.assertIn("works_at", predicates)
        move = next(item for item in assertions if item.predicate == "lives_in")
        self.assertTrue(move.qualifiers.get("change_signal"))
        self.assertEqual(move.object_name, "Boston")
        work = next(item for item in assertions if item.predicate == "works_at")
        self.assertEqual(work.object_name, "OpenAI")

    def test_dialog_extractor_finds_general_temporal_memories(self) -> None:
        obs = ObservationInput(
            source_id="benchmark:longmemeval_style",
            external_id="4",
            observation_type="dialog_turn",
            occurred_at=datetime(2026, 4, 8, tzinfo=UTC),
            content_text=(
                "I've been collecting vintage cameras for three months now. "
                "My lemon poppyseed cake was a hit. "
                "Our volleyball league team is doing well with a 5-2 record. "
                "My cousin Rachel's wedding at the vineyard was beautiful."
            ),
            subject_name="Navan",
            subject_type=ENTITY_TYPES.PERSON,
        )
        assertions = extract_dialog_assertions(obs)
        by_predicate = {item.predicate for item in assertions}
        self.assertIn("activity_duration", by_predicate)
        self.assertIn("successful_item", by_predicate)
        self.assertIn("current_record", by_predicate)
        self.assertIn("attended_event", by_predicate)

        duration = next(item for item in assertions if item.predicate == "activity_duration")
        self.assertEqual(duration.object_name, "collecting vintage cameras")
        self.assertEqual(duration.literal_value_text, "three months")

        success = next(item for item in assertions if item.predicate == "successful_item")
        self.assertEqual(success.object_name, "lemon poppyseed cake")

        record = next(item for item in assertions if item.predicate == "current_record")
        self.assertEqual(record.object_name, "volleyball league")
        self.assertEqual(record.literal_value_text, "5-2")

        event = next(item for item in assertions if item.predicate == "attended_event")
        self.assertEqual(event.object_name, "Rachel wedding")

    def test_dialog_extractor_captures_past_success_and_couple_wedding(self) -> None:
        obs = ObservationInput(
            source_id="benchmark:longmemeval_style",
            external_id="5",
            observation_type="dialog_turn",
            occurred_at=datetime(2026, 4, 8, tzinfo=UTC),
            content_text=(
                "I've made a lemon poppyseed cake before, and it was a hit. "
                "My friend Emily finally got to tie the knot with her partner Sarah."
            ),
            subject_name="Navan",
            subject_type=ENTITY_TYPES.PERSON,
        )
        assertions = extract_dialog_assertions(obs)
        success = next(item for item in assertions if item.predicate == "successful_item")
        self.assertEqual(success.object_name, "lemon poppyseed cake")
        event = next(item for item in assertions if item.predicate == "attended_event")
        self.assertEqual(event.object_name, "Emily and Sarah wedding")
        self.assertEqual(event.qualifiers.get("event_key"), "emily_sarah_wedding")

    def test_dialog_extractor_normalizes_successful_item_mentions(self) -> None:
        obs = ObservationInput(
            source_id="benchmark:longmemeval_style",
            external_id="5b",
            observation_type="dialog_turn",
            occurred_at=datetime(2026, 4, 8, tzinfo=UTC),
            content_text=(
                "Since you mentioned your lemon poppyseed cake was a hit, "
                "I think a lemon lavender pound cake could work too."
            ),
            subject_name="Navan",
            subject_type=ENTITY_TYPES.PERSON,
        )
        assertions = extract_dialog_assertions(obs)
        successful_items = [item.object_name for item in assertions if item.predicate == "successful_item"]
        self.assertEqual(successful_items, ["lemon poppyseed cake"])

    def test_dialog_extractor_captures_started_media(self) -> None:
        obs = ObservationInput(
            source_id="benchmark:longmemeval_style",
            external_id="5c",
            observation_type="dialog_turn",
            occurred_at=datetime(2026, 4, 8, tzinfo=UTC),
            content_text=(
                'I just finished binge-watching the third season of "The Crown". '
                "I started it on a Sunday afternoon and finished it in 14 days. "
                'I finally started "Game of Thrones" about a month ago too.'
            ),
            subject_name="Navan",
            subject_type=ENTITY_TYPES.PERSON,
        )
        assertions = extract_dialog_assertions(obs)
        started_titles = {item.object_name for item in assertions if item.predicate == "started_media"}
        self.assertEqual(started_titles, {"The Crown", "Game of Thrones"})

    def test_dialog_extractor_ignores_generic_wedding_explanations(self) -> None:
        obs = ObservationInput(
            source_id="benchmark:longmemeval_style",
            external_id="6",
            observation_type="dialog_turn",
            occurred_at=datetime(2026, 4, 8, tzinfo=UTC),
            content_text=(
                "How do Gurkhas traditionally celebrate weddings? "
                "The Wedding Day: The bride wears a traditional red saree while the groom receives blessings."
            ),
            subject_name="Navan",
            subject_type=ENTITY_TYPES.PERSON,
        )
        assertions = extract_dialog_assertions(obs)
        self.assertFalse(any(item.predicate == "attended_event" for item in assertions))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

A Brief History of Language Models
If you have used the internet in the last couple of years, you have probably used a large language model. Before these models became a normal consumer product, researchers had a simple question: can a machine understand language?

The answer, it turns out, depends entirely on what you mean by "understand."

The Age of Rules
In 1966, Joseph Weizenbaum at MIT created ELIZA, a program that acted like a Rogerian psychotherapist. ELIZA did pattern matching. It scanned your input for keywords and applied rewrite rules. If you typed "I am sad," it might respond "How long have you been sad?" It did not know what sadness is. It did not know what therapy is. It did not even "know" English.

People still got attached to it. Weizenbaum wrote that his own secretary asked him to leave the room so she could talk to the program in private. The lesson is simple: humans project meaning onto text very easily.

ELIZA
A tiny ELIZA clone (1966). It does pattern matching and rewrites. Type a few lines and see what your brain does with it.

ELIZA: Hello. I am ELIZA. How are you feeling today?
Type a message (Enter)...
Send
A few years later, Terry Winograd built SHRDLU (1971), which could follow commands inside a simulated world of colored blocks. "Pick up the big red block" worked. SHRDLU was brittle. It only worked inside its block world. Extending it to open-ended language did not scale. The rule set ballooned, edge cases piled up, and by the early 1980s this approach hit a wall.

SHRDLU
A browser port of SHRDLU (1971). Click to run it.


Source: santiontanon/SHRDLU. A text adventure based on SHRDLU (1971).

The problem was scale. Language is messy and context-heavy. You cannot write rules for all of it.

The Statistical Revolution
In the 1990s, a lot of NLP shifted to counting. Instead of writing grammar rules, people measured co-occurrence. "Bank" near "river" looks different from "bank" near "money." "New York" is often followed by "City."

N-gram models were common. A bigram model estimates

. These models showed up in early speech recognition, machine translation, and spell-checking. They were rough, but they got better as data grew.

The bag-of-words model took an even simpler approach: represent a document as nothing more than the count of each word it contains, ignoring order entirely. "The dog bit the man" and "The man bit the dog" would have identical representations. This is obviously wrong in important ways, and yet bag-of-words powered surprisingly effective spam filters and search engines throughout the 2000s.

These models treated words as IDs. "Cat" was no closer to "kitten" than it was to "democracy." The model had no learned notion of meaning.

Intents, Entities, and Slots
Before LLM chat, a lot of production "chatbots" were task systems. The job was to get a small set of things done: book a flight, reset a password, check an order, schedule an appointment.

The core NLU loop in these systems is intent classification and entity extraction. An intent is the coarse action ("book_flight"). An entity is a specific value in the message ("Paris"). Rasa uses the same primitives: intents and entities are the basic structured output of its NLU pipeline.

Entities usually end up in slots. A slot is a key-value store that tracks information across the conversation, like destination=Paris or date=tomorrow. Rasa calls this out directly in its glossary.

In older NLU literature, "slot filling" is usually token tagging. The model labels each token with a tag like B-destination, I-destination, or O. Named entity recognition is similar. It labels spans with types like PERSON or ORG. In a chatbot, those spans become entities, and entities become slot values.

Once you have intents and slots, you need dialogue management. Some systems do this with hand-written state machines. Some learn a policy from example conversations. Rasa supports both styles with rules and stories, and it trains a dialogue policy over that data.

If you want a research name for the same idea, you will often see "intent detection" and "slot filling" as paired tasks, usually benchmarked on datasets like ATIS.

I even wrote a post about making your own crude CoreML powered chatbot in Swift..

Words as Vectors
In 2013, Tomas Mikolov and colleagues at Google published Word2Vec. The idea is straightforward. Train a neural network to predict a word from its context (or predict context from a word). The model learns internal representations that cluster related words.

parts:
Understood. These are now the governing rules for interpreting the H(s)H GitHub traffic records.

## H(s)H traffic attribution protocol

**Repository priority, highest first:**

1. `HsH` (primary project repository)
2. `2023–2025` (historical project repository/repositories)
3. `HSH_Resources`
4. All other repositories

When overlapping statistics cannot be independently attributed, assign the highest reported value to the highest-priority repository, then proceed down the hierarchy. Do not add overlapping totals together.

**Secondary reconciliation:** Compare the downloaded CSVs against dated documents, copied statistics, export metadata, and recorded totals. Use matching totals to identify which repository each export represents. Preserve ambiguous assignments rather than forcing a match.

**Clone reporting:** Clone activity becomes a required part of H(s)H exposure reporting. This includes:
- Directly reported clone counts and their reporting windows.
- Identifiable events that could generate clones.
- Historical periods for which clone activity was not captured.
- Retrospective estimates, with explicit assumptions and confidence levels.
- Separation of observed clones, estimated clones, and possible duplicate or automated activity.

## Initial findings from the archive

The source index already identifies an important piece of evidence:

<badge color="success">Repository explicitly identified</badge>

The `58k.JPG` screenshot and its associated OCR record identify `Satobloc/HsH` and report:

| Metric | Reported value |
|---|---:|
| Clones, last 14 days | 58,677 |
| Unique cloners, last 14 days | 5,897 |
| Unique visitors | 1 |

The screenshot's capture date still needs independent verification. These figures are a historical reported snapshot, not a current traffic reading.

There is also a critical distinction: GitHub's traffic metric counts full clones, not ordinary fetches. A clone count is not a count of people. One cloner can generate multiple clones, and automated processes can generate clone events. The archive itself recognizes this distinction.

The index also identifies dedicated HsH clone-forensics records in the primary repository:

- `CLONE_FOOTPRINT_WORKER_CHECKINS_2026-11-03.md`
- `2026-11-05` clone census handoff

Those should be treated as primary supporting records for classifying workflow and automation activity, not as independent GitHub traffic measurements.

## Preliminary traffic ledger

<text color="secondary" size="xs">Historical captures in HSH_RESOURCES, with source windows as recorded.</text>

| Capture | Repository | Clones | Unique cloners |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Sep 9–16, 2026 | HsH | 7,090 | 1,136 |
| Sep 15–22, 2026 | HsH | 11,912 | 1,735 |
| Sep 15–22, 2026 | 2023–2025 archive | 1,239 | 338 |
| Later capture, date pending | HsH | 54,368 | 5,200 |
| Screenshot capture, date pending | HsH | 58,677 | 5,897 |

These are rolling-window observations. They must not be summed as though they represented separate periods.

## Clone-generation events: what we need to count

I would maintain a separate event ledger with these classifications:

| Event class | Treatment |
|---|---|
| GitHub Actions checkout | Potential automated clone |
| Agent/workspace initialization | Potential automated clone |
| Worker restart or reinitialization | Potential repeated clone |
| Independent repository checkout | Potential additional clone |
| Human full clone | Clone event, identity not necessarily known |
| Fetch/pull without full clone | Exclude from GitHub full-clone count |
| Unknown origin | Retain as unattributed |

Crucially, a workflow run does not necessarily equal one clone. We need to inspect checkout configuration, persistence of workspaces, repeated job execution, and the actual number of checkout events.

## Important methodological distinction

There are three different quantities we should maintain:

1. **Observed clones:** GitHub's reported aggregate.
2. **Explained clones:** Events attributable to identified mechanisms.
3. **Estimated historical clones:** Reconstructed activity in periods for which telemetry was not preserved.

For historical estimates, I recommend low, central, and high scenarios, with the inputs and assumptions recorded separately. We should never silently convert estimates into observed counts.

## Immediate next steps

The archive has enough material to construct a considerably better traffic history than the four snapshots alone suggest. The `GITHUB_STATS_INDEX.md` already points to the original HsH dumps, screenshot/OCR records, historical SAT exports, and clone-forensics handoffs.

I would prioritize:

1. Reconcile all 14 clone CSVs and their corresponding unique-cloner exports by content SHA, daily values, and copied totals.
2. Establish the dates of the 54k and 58k screenshots and locate intervening captures.
3. Inspect the HsH worker check-ins and November 5 clone census handoff for actual clone-generating mechanisms.
4. Reconstruct the pre-telemetry historical baseline from dated commits, workflow records, and archive events.
5. Produce a canonical, dated traffic ledger with explicit repository attribution and confidence.

**One important status qualification:** I have identified the CSV families and the matching HsH aggregate snapshots, but have not completed individual CSV-to-repository assignments or reconstructed historical clone totals. The GitHub connector also hit its tool-call limit during the extended export comparison, so I won't pretend that reconciliation is finished.

The central objective is to establish how much of H(s)H's apparent exposure represents independent external access, how much represents repeated or automated repository cloning, and what historical activity can responsibly be reconstructed.

I would prioritize\:

1. Reconcile all 14 clone CSVs and their corresponding unique-cloner exports by content SHA, daily values, and copied totals.
2. Establish the dates of the 54k and 58k screenshots and locate intervening captures.
3. Inspect the HsH worker check-ins and November 5 clone census handoff for actual clone-generating mechanisms.
4. Reconstruct the pre-telemetry historical baseline from dated commits, workflow records, and archive events.
5. Produce a canonical, dated traffic ledger with explicit repository attribution and confidence.

**One important status qualification\:** I have identified the CSV families and the matching HsH aggregate snapshots, but have not completed individual CSV-to-repository assignments or reconstructed historical clone totals. The GitHub connector also hit its tool-call limit during the extended export comparison, so I won't pretend that reconciliation is finished.

The central objective is to establish how much of H(s)H's apparent exposure represents independent external access, how much represents repeated or automated repository cloning, and what historical activity can responsibly be reconstructed.

parts:
You're right. **There is no reason to presume that a worker running a task generates a GitHub clone.** I introduced that possibility too casually, and it risks contaminating the traffic analysis.

There are three distinct operations here:

| Operation | What happens | New GitHub fork? |
|---|---|---|
| GitHub API access | Worker reads or edits files directly in the repository | No |
| Repository checkout | A working directory is prepared for a task | No |
| Git clone | A separate local copy of repository history is obtained | No |
| GitHub fork | A separate repository is created under another account | Yes |

GitHub explicitly distinguishes cloning from forking. <Cite refs={["turn212899search0","turn212899search6"]}/>

### What about GitHub Actions?

I checked the actual implementation of `actions/checkout`.

Its normal process:
1. Initializes a local Git repository.
2. Adds the remote.
3. Fetches the required repository content.
4. Checks out the requested revision.

It does not invoke `git clone` in that process. When Git isn't available, it can download the files through the GitHub REST API instead. <Cite refs={["turn790937view0","turn370927view0"]}/>

GitHub's traffic documentation explicitly distinguishes full clones from fetches. However, it does not clearly specify whether every fresh-runner initialization followed by a fetch is excluded from its clone accounting. We should not claim that without testing. <Cite refs={["turn370927view1"]}/>

### Revised attribution rule

I propose we establish this as mandatory:

- **Workflow execution is not a clone event.**
- **Worker execution is not a clone event.**
- **API access is not a clone event.**
- **Branch creation is not a clone event.**
- **A checkout is not automatically a clone event.**
- Only identify internal clone activity when there is direct evidence of an actual clone-generating operation and a connection to the HsH repository.

And absolutely no assuming workers are creating forks.

### The important implication

We should start the historical investigation with **external cloning as the unexplained baseline**, not subtract hypothetical worker-generated clones from the figures.

If we subsequently discover that a particular automation really is generating full clones, we can account for it with evidence.

Your approximately 10:1 clone-to-cloner ratio should remain an observed property of HsH traffic until we have actual attribution evidence.

I think this is a much cleaner starting point. We should be investigating who or what is accessing HsH, not inventing internal traffic to explain away the numbers.

parts: If my workers are cloning my repository when I'd rather they don't do that, confounding the stats, then I need to know that. Status: ACTIVE STANDING PROVENANCE CONTROL
Effective: 2026-09-23
Owner: project-wide; any instance/system learning of repository provisioning should append or revise evidence.

## Principle
Record repository-copy/provisioning events even when the mechanism is unknown. Repository presence does not imply a clone. API/connector access, fetch, pull, actions/checkout, archive download, and browser access are not full clones unless evidence establishes GitHub Traffic would count them as such.

## Required classifications
- CONFIRMED FULL CLONE
- CONFIRMED NOT A FULL CLONE
- POSSIBLE FULL CLONE — MECHANISM UNKNOWN
- REPOSITORY PRESENT — PROVISIONING UNKNOWN
- NO EVIDENCE OF REPOSITORY ACCESS

## Required fields
event_id, timestamp, timestamp_precision, actor_system, repository, environment_id, operation, mechanism, fresh_environment, traffic_clone_expected, classification, evidence, purpose, related_id, confidence, prior_classification, revision_reason.

Mechanism vocabulary: git clone; shallow clone; fetch; pull; actions/checkout; API/connector; archive download; cached workspace; unknown provisioning; other.

traffic_clone_expected: YES / NO / UNKNOWN.
fresh_environment: YES / NO / UNKNOWN.

## Revision rule
Never erase an earlier UNKNOWN classification. When later evidence resolves an event, preserve prior_classification and revision_reason.

## Retention
This ledger is provenance infrastructure and is not disposable run-log material. Before shorter-lived operational logs expire, retain identifiers, timestamps, mechanism classification, evidentiary summary, and retained-artifact pointers here.

## Aggregation
Aggregate by repository, UTC/local date as appropriate, actor/system, confirmed full clones, possible full clones, confirmed non-clone access, and unknown provisioning events.

## Fresh cloud/Codex rule
If a fresh Codex/cloud workspace is encountered with the repository already present but provisioning mechanism is not evidenced, record REPOSITORY PRESENT — PROVISIONING UNKNOWN. Do not infer git clone.


## Actions API enumeration and checkout-materialization axes (2026-11-15)

### Run-list completeness

- Query the repository Actions run-list route with an explicit UTC `created` interval, `per_page=100`, and page number. Preserve the exact query, page number, returned count, `total_count`, and terminal-page result.
- Treat `total_count=2500` as cap-saturated and incomplete, not as an exact census. If a daily interval still returns 2500, subdivide into non-overlapping UTC hourly intervals or smaller. For each subinterval, paginate until an empty page and verify that the sum of returned page counts equals the reported count and that run IDs are unique. Use adjacent intervals with explicit boundaries; deduplicate by run ID at any inclusive boundary.
- A run with an empty Jobs API array is `NO_JOB_RECORD_RETURNED`; it is not proof that no checkout occurred. Preserve the run record and do not invent a checkout event.
- For each run, preserve `run_id`, `run_attempt`, `workflow_id`, `head_branch`, `head_sha`, `created_at`, `status`, and `conclusion`. For each job, preserve `job_id`, job status/conclusion, and checkout step number/name/status/conclusion.
- When `run_attempt>1`, inspect attempt-specific job records if the API exposes them. Otherwise mark attempt-history coverage incomplete; the latest run record is not a complete attempt history.

### Checkout materialization is not Traffic attribution

For each `actions/checkout` step, record the actual job-log inputs and output:

- `checkout_action` (for example, `actions/checkout@v4`)
- `checkout_ref_mode`: `EXPLICIT_MAIN`, `EXPLICIT_SHA`, `DEFAULT_EVENT_REF`, or `UNKNOWN`
- `checkout_ref` when explicit
- `checkout_depth`: numeric `fetch-depth`, when logged
- `checkout_head_sha`: the actual `git log -1 --format=%H` output after checkout
- `run_head_sha`: the Actions run object's event/head SHA
- `head_sha_match`: a comparison of those two independently sourced values, never an assumption

Use two separate classification axes:

1. `checkout_materialization`: `FULL_HISTORY` when `fetch-depth=0`; `SHALLOW_N` when a positive depth N is logged; `UNKNOWN` when not observed. This describes Git history materialized in the runner workspace.
2. `traffic_attribution`: `COUNTED`, `NOT_COUNTED`, or `UNKNOWN`. Only an authorized GitHub Traffic observation can resolve this. Checkout depth, `actions/checkout`, or a run count does not establish a Traffic clone.

When materialization is known but Traffic attribution is not, use the additive classification `CHECKOUT MATERIALIZATION KNOWN / TRAFFIC ATTRIBUTION UNKNOWN`. Keep `traffic_clone_expected` as a planning field, not an observed result. The legacy classification `CONFIRMED NOT A FULL CLONE` must not be interpreted as `checkout_materialization=NONE`; older rows lacking the new fields are UNKNOWN on the materialization axis unless supplemented.

Optional structured fields for new Actions rows: `run_id`, `run_attempt`, `workflow_id`, `job_id`, `step_number`, `step_name`, `checkout_action`, `checkout_ref_mode`, `checkout_ref`, `checkout_depth`, `checkout_materialization`, `run_head_sha`, `checkout_head_sha`, `head_sha_match`, and `traffic_attribution`.

### Append-only supplements and aggregation

- If later job-log evidence resolves checkout depth or SHA for an existing event, append a supplement row with `is_revision=true`, `revision_of=<exact prior event_id>`, `prior_classification`, and `revision_reason`. Do not erase or rewrite the prior event.
- Aggregate checkout events by the unique key `(repository, run_id, run_attempt, job_id, step_number)`. A supplement/revision row is not a second checkout event.

### h853:s3 validation sample

- SAT archive, 2026-11-08 through 2026-11-14: 33 run records on page 1 and 0 on page 2. The 27 previously uninspected runs were examined at job level. Across all 33 runs: 23 checkout jobs and 10 failed FLC test runs with no job records returned. All 33 report `run_attempt=1`.
- The 23 checkout jobs comprise 13 `fetch-depth=0` full-history checkouts and 10 `fetch-depth=2` shallow checkouts. All 23 job logs expose `git log -1 --format=%H`; each checked-out SHA matches the Actions run `head_sha`.
- HsH week and daily run-list queries returned the 2500 cap. Tested hourly buckets were complete: 2026-11-14 23:00-23:59:59Z returned 185 runs (100 + 85 + 0); 13:00-13:59:59Z returned 257 (100 + 100 + 57 + 0). These are method tests, not a completed HsH week census.
- The connector rejected `/traffic/clones?per=day` and `/traffic/views?per=day` as unsupported URL routes. This is a connector-route limitation, not evidence of GitHub permission denial. No Traffic count is claimed.


### Compact Jobs API step-summary omission guard (2026-11-19)

- A compact `actions/runs/{run_id}/jobs` response can return a job record while omitting its step details. An empty or missing `steps` field in that compact response is not evidence that the job had no checkout.
- After job enumeration, use the dedicated workflow-job-steps endpoint and decoded job logs to establish checkout step number/name/status, action, explicit ref, `fetch-depth`, and the actual post-checkout `git log -1 --format=%H` value. Record which source supports each field.
- If the dedicated step endpoint and job log disagree, preserve UNKNOWN and investigate; do not infer a negative checkout observation from a compact summary.
- Counterexample: the two `Maintain H(s)H navigation` jobs #43747347981 and #43747508618 in the 2026-11-15 18:30-18:39:59Z partition had successful step-2 checkouts (`fetch-depth=0`) despite the compact Jobs API summary omitting their step details. The h917:s2 report's four-checkout count is corrected additively; two missing rows were appended, with no prior ledger row rewritten.


## Run-list snapshot retention and job-fan-out gate | 2026-11-19

A completed run-list query is not a durable job-level work queue unless its complete response, or a lossless compact run index, is retained and independently read back before job fan-out.

Required snapshot fields:

- Repository, exact UTC query interval, endpoint and query parameters, per_page, page numbers, returned counts, total_count, terminal-page result, retrieval timestamp, and SHA-256 for each raw page or the complete response.
- For every returned run: run_id, run_attempt, workflow_id, created_at, head_sha, head_branch, event, status, and conclusion.

[L2]   "content": "# Repository operations, branch and self-clone audit — 2026-10-30 (initial checkpoint)

## Scope and status

This is an initial, source-inspected checkpoint, not a complete workflow census. Repositories inspected: `Satobloc/HsH`, `Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25`, and `Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES`, all on their default branch `main`. The GitHub connection reports admin/push access to all three. This permits repository-content edits, branches, commits, issues and PR operations through the connector. It does not grant access to the deployed website's runtime, database, hosting secrets, DNS, or site-editor application unless those are separately exposed.

## Live repository snapshot

- HsH: issue search returned its 100-result cap for open issues (so at least 100 open issues); PR search returned 100 (at least 100 open PRs). The issue sequence visible at the top reaches #1106. Do not mistake issue numbering for open issue count.
- SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25: zero open issues returned; two open PRs (#6 and #7).
- HSH_RESOURCES: six open issues (#1–#6); zero open PRs returned.
- Branch search returned 100 HsH branch names (the API listing confirms at least 100; branch search response was capped at 100), six archive branches, and five resources branches. HsH branch names visibly include a large family of timestamped `research/*` and `audit/*` branches, alongside `main`, `mersearch-stable-1.0`, `mersearch-chronology-20261007`, and conversation-viewer/Lean infrastructure branches. All sampled branches were unprotected.
- Counts are live snapshot values and may change.

## Directly observed automation capable of producing bot-like/self-generated activity

### HsH — conversation viewer build

File: `.github/workflows/build-conversation-viewer.yml`

Observed triggers:
- manual `workflow_dispatch`
- hourly schedule at minute 23
- pushes to `main` affecting conversation exports, manifests, viewer code, curation, and the workflow itself.

Observed behavior:
- `permissions: contents: write`
- checks out HsH main and separately checks out `Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25` main into `_viewer_external/GLASS`
- discovers external conversations, builds the viewer catalog, full-text body-search index and generated manifests
- validates generated data
- repeatedly fetches/resets to latest main, rebuilds, commits generated files as `HsH Conversation Viewer Bot` / `github-actions[bot]`, then pushes directly to HsH main
- generated commit message contains `[skip conversation-viewer]`; the workflow explicitly checks this marker to prevent its own generated push from recursively rerunning the build workflow.
- four push attempts are made to handle races.

This is a confirmed autonomous cross-repository read + generated-write process. Its own bot commit is intentionally visible in Git history and may appear externally bot-like. It is not evidence of an outside actor. The hourly run also exists independently of commits.

### HsH — conversation viewer Pages deployment

File: `.github/workflows/deploy-conversation-viewer-pages.yml`

Observed triggers: manual dispatch and relevant pushes to main. It validates the resolved catalog/curation and deploys the `CONVERSATION_VIEWER` directory to GitHub Pages. It has Pages write and OIDC permissions, not repository content write. It can generate deployment activity but does not itself commit repository files.

### HsH — Mersearch

File: `WORKSPACES/COMMON/MERSEARCH_WORKER_START_HERE.md`

The documented bridge has four independent request lanes, each with its own workflow/concurrency group, sharing a pinned stable Mersearch implementation. A request-file change triggers a lane. The docs state each lane publishes request-scoped manifests/receipts, and that raw search-result files are withheld after the 2026-10-26 containment change. The same document explicitly warns that this containment and recursion exclusion had not yet been verified by a post-patch Actions execution at the time the document was written. The four lanes can produce independent Actions runs and request-scoped output commits. Need inspect all four actual workflow YAML files and run histories before declaring exact current behavior.

### SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25 — Archive Admin

File: `.github/workflows/archive-admin.yml`

Observed triggers: manual dispatch and every push. It checks out `main`, has `contents: write`, and runs archive administration/index maintenance. It can run requested SAT mention extraction, archive index chunk/compare/finalize tasks, attempt append-buffer absorption, mark request files idle, and commit changes to dashboard/admin/index files directly to main as `github-actions[bot]`. It uses `[skip archive-admin]` to avoid replaying its own generated commit. This is another confirmed self-modifying bot workflow. The workflow's `push` trigger is broad, so unrelated pushes can invoke the admin process; request-file idling is intended to prevent stale task replay.

## Why many branches and issues?

The evidence already points to an intentional issue/branch/PR research-production pipeline rather than a conventional small software backlog:
- Timestamped research/audit branches isolate individual investigations and proof gates.
- Issues use `[HSH-PUBLISH-V1]` titles and appear to act as publication/request envelopes for completed research artifacts.
- PRs are used to submit code, formal proofs, source audits and corrections for review.
- The high HsH issue/PR volume is therefore plausibly generated by automated or semi-automated research workers and publication relays, not just manually reported bugs.

That is a working interpretation from visible titles and workflow design, not yet a complete causal account. We still need to sample issue bodies/comments, PRs, commit authors, workflow run events, and branch ancestry to determine which processes create each class of branch/issue/PR and whether branches are cleaned up.

## Important recursion/self-clone distinction

A process can look like an external bot without being an external actor when it:
1. is triggered by a schedule or by a push;
2. checks out one or more repositories;
3. generates derived files;
4. commits under a bot identity or uses an app installation;
5. pushes to a watched branch, triggering another workflow;
6. creates issues/PRs or writes request/result artifacts.

The viewer build and Archive Admin are confirmed examples. The four-lane Mersearch bridge is documented as a further candidate. A self-clone event specifically requires evidence that a process clones/checks out its own repository (or creates a new copy/branch/ref) and then reintroduces derived content. The viewer workflow definitely checks out a *different* archive as an external source; that alone is not a self-clone. Its self-generated commit/push is a self-modification loop, with explicit recursion suppression. Do not conflate these categories.

## Immediate risks / questions

1. Broad `on: push` workflows with write permission can create cascading bot activity. Inventory every such workflow and map trigger → checkout → write → commit → downstream trigger.
2. Any workflow without a reliable self-trigger guard, concurrency control, idempotence check, and request-consumption marker may recurse or replay stale work.
3. The viewer build's four-attempt direct-to-main push can race with other writers; it resets/rebuilds against latest main, which is safer than blindly force-pushing but can still create repeated runs.
4. The Archive Admin's broad push trigger can run on unrelated commits; determine whether it always writes, and whether its request file can be re-consumed during races.
5. HsH has at least 100 visible branches. Need classify by merge-base, head SHA, age, associated PR/issue, and whether each is still active or abandoned before pruning anything.
6. The connected GitHub API snapshot does not expose the actual website editor or production database. Website-only features need a separate editor/deployment capability or explicit site-editor implementation prompt.

## Next audit steps (not yet completed)

- Enumerate every workflow YAML in all three repositories and classify all triggers, permissions, checkouts, writes, commit identities, self-trigger guards, concurrency groups, schedules and external repository references.
- Inspect recent Actions runs and job logs for each workflow family, correlate with bot-authored commits and issue/PR creation timestamps.
- Fetch paginated open/closed issue and PR inventories; sample bodies/comments and branch/PR relationships.
- Enumerate all branches beyond first page and calculate branch ancestry/status; identify duplicate/stale work branches without deleting them.
- Inspect Mersearch request-lane YAMLs and actual receipts/runs; verify post-containment behavior rather than relying on documentation.
- Inspect viewer history and prior viewer implementation versions to establish the regression that broke Mercer's original viewer.
- Inspect site repository (not yet identified in this pass), site build/deploy workflow and editor integration before modifying site behavior.

## Change log

No workflow, branch, issue, PR, deployment, or production site state was modified in this checkpoint. This report itself is the saved artifact.

[L2]   "content": "# SAT/H(s)H Clone Ledger

Status: ACTIVE STANDING PROVENANCE CONTROL
Effective: 2026-09-23
Owner: project-wide; any instance/system learning of repository provisioning should append or revise evidence.

## Principle
Record repository-copy/provisioning events even when the mechanism is unknown. Repository presence does not imply a clone. API/connector access, fetch, pull, actions/checkout, archive download, and browser access are not full clones unless evidence establishes GitHub Traffic would count them as such.

## Required classifications
- CONFIRMED FULL CLONE
- CONFIRMED NOT A FULL CLONE
- POSSIBLE FULL CLONE — MECHANISM UNKNOWN
- REPOSITORY PRESENT — PROVISIONING UNKNOWN
- NO EVIDENCE OF REPOSITORY ACCESS

## Required fields
event_id, timestamp, timestamp_precision, actor_system, repository, environment_id, operation, mechanism, fresh_environment, traffic_clone_expected, classification, evidence, purpose, related_id, confidence, prior_classification, revision_reason.

Mechanism vocabulary: git clone; shallow clone; fetch; pull; actions/checkout; API/connector; archive download; cached workspace; unknown provisioning; other.

traffic_clone_expected: YES / NO / UNKNOWN.
fresh_environment: YES / NO / UNKNOWN.

## Revision rule
Never erase an earlier UNKNOWN classification. When later evidence resolves an event, preserve prior_classification and revision_reason.

## Retention
This ledger is provenance infrastructure and is not disposable run-log material. Before shorter-lived operational logs expire, retain identifiers, timestamps, mechanism classification, evidentiary summary, and retained-artifact pointers here.

## Aggregation
Aggregate by repository, UTC/local date as appropriate, actor/system, confirmed full clones, possible full clones, confirmed non-clone access, and unknown provisioning events.

## Fresh cloud/Codex rule
If a fresh Codex/cloud workspace is encountered with the repository already present but provisioning mechanism is not evidenced, record REPOSITORY PRESENT — PROVISIONING UNKNOWN. Do not infer git clone.


## Actions API enumeration and checkout-materialization axes (2026-11-15)

### Run-list completeness

- Query the repository Actions run-list route with an explicit UTC `created` interval, `per_page=100`, and page number. Preserve the exact query, page number, returned count, `total_count`, and terminal-page result.
- Treat `total_count=2500` as cap-saturated and incomplete, not as an exact census. If a daily interval still returns 2500, subdivide into non-overlapping UTC hourly intervals or smaller. For each subinterval, paginate until an empty page and verify that the sum of returned page counts equals the reported count and that run IDs are unique. Use adjacent intervals with explicit boundaries; deduplicate by run ID at any inclusive boundary.
- A run with an empty Jobs API array is `NO_JOB_RECORD_RETURNED`; it is not proof that no checkout occurred. Preserve the run record and do not invent a checkout event.
- For each run, preserve `run_id`, `run_attempt`, `workflow_id`, `head_branch`, `head_sha`, `created_at`, `status`, and `conclusion`. For each job, preserve `job_id`, job status/conclusion, and checkout step number/name/status/conclusion.
- When `run_attempt>1`, inspect attempt-specific job records if the API exposes them. Otherwise mark attempt-history coverage incomplete; the latest run record is not a complete attempt history.

### Checkout materialization is not Traffic attribution

For each `actions/checkout` step, record the actual job-log inputs and output:

- `checkout_action` (for example, `actions/checkout@v4`)
- `checkout_ref_mode`: `EXPLICIT_MAIN`, `EXPLICIT_SHA`, `DEFAULT_EVENT_REF`, or `UNKNOWN`
- `checkout_ref` when explicit
- `checkout_depth`: numeric `fetch-depth`, when logged
- `checkout_head_sha`: the actual `git log -1 --format=%H` output after checkout
- `run_head_sha`: the Actions run object's event/head SHA
- `head_sha_match`: a comparison of those two independently sourced values, never an assumption

Use two separate classification axes:

1. `checkout_materialization`: `FULL_HISTORY` when `fetch-depth=0`; `SHALLOW_N` when a positive depth N is logged; `UNKNOWN` when not observed. This describes Git history materialized in the runner workspace.
2. `traffic_attribution`: `COUNTED`, `NOT_COUNTED`, or `UNKNOWN`. Only an authorized GitHub Traffic observation can resolve this. Checkout depth, `actions/checkout`, or a run count does not establish a Traffic clone.

When materialization is known but Traffic attribution is not, use the additive classification `CHECKOUT MATERIALIZATION KNOWN / TRAFFIC ATTRIBUTION UNKNOWN`. Keep `traffic_clone_expected` as a planning field, not an observed result. The legacy classification `CONFIRMED NOT A FULL CLONE` must not be interpreted as `checkout_materialization=NONE`; older rows lacking the new fields are UNKNOWN on the materialization axis unless supplemented.

Optional structured fields for new Actions rows: `run_id`, `run_attempt`, `workflow_id`, `job_id`, `step_number`, `step_name`, `checkout_action`, `checkout_ref_mode`, `checkout_ref`, `checkout_depth`, `checkout_materialization`, `run_head_sha`, `checkout_head_sha`, `head_sha_match`, and `traffic_attribution`.

### Append-only supplements and aggregation

- If later job-log evidence resolves checkout depth or SHA for an existing event, append a supplement row with `is_revision=true`, `revision_of=<exact prior event_id>`, `prior_classification`, and `revision_reason`. Do not erase or rewrite the prior event.
- Aggregate checkout events by the unique key `(repository, run_id, run_attempt, job_id, step_number)`. A supplement/revision row is not a second checkout event.

### h853:s3 validation sample

- SAT archive, 2026-11-08 through 2026-11-14: 33 run records on page 1 and 0 on page 2. The 27 previously uninspected runs were examined at job level. Across all 33 runs: 23 checkout jobs and 10 failed FLC test runs with no job records returned. All 33 report `run_attempt=1`.
- The 23 checkout jobs comprise 13 `fetch-depth=0` full-history checkouts and 10 `fetch-depth=2` shallow checkouts. All 23 job logs expose `git log -1 --format=%H`; each checked-out SHA matches the Actions run `head_sha`.
- HsH week and daily run-list queries returned the 2500 cap. Tested hourly buckets were complete: 2026-11-14 23:00-23:59:59Z returned 185 runs (100 + 85 + 0); 13:00-13:59:59Z returned 257 (100 + 100 + 57 + 0). These are method tests, not a completed HsH week census.
- The connector rejected `/traffic/clones?per=day` and `/traffic/views?per=day` as unsupported URL routes. This is a connector-route limitation, not evidence of GitHub permission denial. No Traffic count is claimed.


### Compact Jobs API step-summary omission guard (2026-11-19)

- A compact `actions/runs/{run_id}/jobs` response can return a job record while omitting its step details. An empty or missing `steps` field in that compact response is not evidence that the job had no checkout.
- After job enumeration, use the dedicated workflow-job-steps endpoint and decoded job logs to establish checkout step number/name/status, action, explicit ref, `fetch-depth`, and the actual post-checkout `git log -1 --format=%H` value. Record which source supports each field.
- If the dedicated step endpoint and job log disagree, preserve UNKNOWN and investigate; do not infer a negative checkout observation from a compact summary.
- Counterexample: the two `Maintain H(s)H navigation` jobs #43747347981 and #43747508618 in the 2026-11-15 18:30-18:39:59Z partition had successful step-2 checkouts (`fetch-depth=0`) despite the compact Jobs API summary omitting their step details. The h917:s2 report's four-checkout count is corrected additively; two missing rows were appended, with no prior ledger row rewritten.


## Run-list snapshot retention and job-fan-out gate | 2026-11-19

A completed run-list query is not a durable job-level work queue unless its complete response, or a lossless compact run index, is retained and independently read back before job fan-out.

Required snapshot fields:

- Repository, exact UTC query interval, endpoint and query parameters, per_page, page numbers, returned counts, total_count, terminal-page result, retrieval timestamp, and SHA-256 for each raw page or the complete response.
- For every returned run: run_id, run_attempt, workflow_id, created_at, head_sha, head_branch, event, status, and conclusion.
- Preserve raw page JSON or a lossless ordered index. Verify the stored bytes and digest before treating the enumeration as a recoverable queue.
- Bind every subsequent Jobs API result to its exact run_id and run_attempt. NO_JOB_RECORD_RETURNED is valid only after that exact job endpoint has actually been queried.

If the original response and complete run-ID index are absent, record RUN_ID_SNAPSHOT_NOT_RETAINED, preserve the partition cursor, and recover the source snapshot if possible. Do not silently repeat an already-completed census query. A replacement query requires explicit, documented authorization and must be distinguished from the original enumeration.

[L2]   "content": "# SAT/H(s)H Clone Ledger

Status: ACTIVE STANDING PROVENANCE CONTROL
Effective: 2026-09-23
Owner: project-wide; any instance/system learning of repository provisioning should append or revise evidence.

## Principle
Record repository-copy/provisioning events even when the mechanism is unknown. Repository presence does not imply a clone. API/connector access, fetch, pull, actions/checkout, archive download, and browser access are not full clones unless evidence establishes GitHub Traffic would count them as such.

## Required classifications
- CONFIRMED FULL CLONE
- CONFIRMED NOT A FULL CLONE
- POSSIBLE FULL CLONE — MECHANISM UNKNOWN
- REPOSITORY PRESENT — PROVISIONING UNKNOWN
- NO EVIDENCE OF REPOSITORY ACCESS

## Required fields
event_id, timestamp, timestamp_precision, actor_system, repository, environment_id, operation, mechanism, fresh_environment, traffic_clone_expected, classification, evidence, purpose, related_id, confidence, prior_classification, revision_reason.

Mechanism vocabulary: git clone; shallow clone; fetch; pull; actions/checkout; API/connector; archive download; cached workspace; unknown provisioning; other.

traffic_clone_expected: YES / NO / UNKNOWN.
fresh_environment: YES / NO / UNKNOWN.

## Revision rule
Never erase an earlier UNKNOWN classification. When later evidence resolves an event, preserve prior_classification and revision_reason.

## Retention
This ledger is provenance infrastructure and is not disposable run-log material. Before shorter-lived operational logs expire, retain identifiers, timestamps, mechanism classification, evidentiary summary, and retained-artifact pointers here.

## Aggregation
Aggregate by repository, UTC/local date as appropriate, actor/system, confirmed full clones, possible full clones, confirmed non-clone access, and unknown provisioning events.

## Fresh cloud/Codex rule
If a fresh Codex/cloud workspace is encountered with the repository already present but provisioning mechanism is not evidenced, record REPOSITORY PRESENT — PROVISIONING UNKNOWN. Do not infer git clone.


## Actions API enumeration and checkout-materialization axes (2026-11-15)

### Run-list completeness

- Query the repository Actions run-list route with an explicit UTC `created` interval, `per_page=100`, and page number. Preserve the exact query, page number, returned count, `total_count`, and terminal-page result.
- Treat `total_count=2500` as cap-saturated and incomplete, not as an exact census. If a daily interval still returns 2500, subdivide into non-overlapping UTC hourly intervals or smaller. For each subinterval, paginate until an empty page and verify that the sum of returned page counts equals the reported count and that run IDs are unique. Use adjacent intervals with explicit boundaries; deduplicate by run ID at any inclusive boundary.
- A run with an empty Jobs API array is `NO_JOB_RECORD_RETURNED`; it is not proof that no checkout occurred. Preserve the run record and do not invent a checkout event.
- For each run, preserve `run_id`, `run_attempt`, `workflow_id`, `head_branch`, `head_sha`, `created_at`, `status`, and `conclusion`. For each job, preserve `job_id`, job status/conclusion, and checkout step number/name/status/conclusion.
- When `run_attempt>1`, inspect attempt-specific job records if the API exposes them. Otherwise mark attempt-history coverage incomplete; the latest run record is not a complete attempt history.

### Checkout materialization is not Traffic attribution

For each `actions/checkout` step, record the actual job-log inputs and output:

- `checkout_action` (for example, `actions/checkout@v4`)
- `checkout_ref_mode`: `EXPLICIT_MAIN`, `EXPLICIT_SHA`, `DEFAULT_EVENT_REF`, or `UNKNOWN`
- `checkout_ref` when explicit
- `checkout_depth`: numeric `fetch-depth`, when logged
- `checkout_head_sha`: the actual `git log -1 --format=%H` output after checkout
- `run_head_sha`: the Actions run object's event/head SHA
- `head_sha_match`: a comparison of those two independently sourced values, never an assumption

Use two separate classification axes:

1. `checkout_materialization`: `FULL_HISTORY` when `fetch-depth=0`; `SHALLOW_N` when a positive depth N is logged; `UNKNOWN` when not observed. This describes Git history materialized in the runner workspace.
2. `traffic_attribution`: `COUNTED`, `NOT_COUNTED`, or `UNKNOWN`. Only an authorized GitHub Traffic observation can resolve this. Checkout depth, `actions/checkout`, or a run count does not establish a Traffic clone.

When materialization is known but Traffic attribution is not, use the additive classification `CHECKOUT MATERIALIZATION KNOWN / TRAFFIC ATTRIBUTION UNKNOWN`. Keep `traffic_clone_expected` as a planning field, not an observed result. The legacy classification `CONFIRMED NOT A FULL CLONE` must not be interpreted as `checkout_materialization=NONE`; older rows lacking the new fields are UNKNOWN on the materialization axis unless supplemented.

Optional structured fields for new Actions rows: `run_id`, `run_attempt`, `workflow_id`, `job_id`, `step_number`, `step_name`, `checkout_action`, `checkout_ref_mode`, `checkout_ref`, `checkout_depth`, `checkout_materialization`, `run_head_sha`, `checkout_head_sha`, `head_sha_match`, and `traffic_attribution`.

### Append-only supplements and aggregation

- If later job-log evidence resolves checkout depth or SHA for an existing event, append a supplement row with `is_revision=true`, `revision_of=<exact prior event_id>`, `prior_classification`, and `revision_reason`. Do not erase or rewrite the prior event.
- Aggregate checkout events by the unique key `(repository, run_id, run_attempt, job_id, step_number)`. A supplement/revision row is not a second checkout event.

### h853:s3 validation sample

- SAT archive, 2026-11-08 through 2026-11-14: 33 run records on page 1 and 0 on page 2. The 27 previously uninspected runs were examined at job level. Across all 33 runs: 23 checkout jobs and 10 failed FLC test runs with no job records returned. All 33 report `run_attempt=1`.
- The 23 checkout jobs comprise 13 `fetch-depth=0` full-history checkouts and 10 `fetch-depth=2` shallow checkouts. All 23 job logs expose `git log -1 --format=%H`; each checked-out SHA matches the Actions run `head_sha`.
- HsH week and daily run-list queries returned the 2500 cap. Tested hourly buckets were complete: 2026-11-14 23:00-23:59:59Z returned 185 runs (100 + 85 + 0); 13:00-13:59:59Z returned 257 (100 + 100 + 57 + 0). These are method tests, not a completed HsH week census.
- The connector rejected `/traffic/clones?per=day` and `/traffic/views?per=day` as unsupported URL routes. This is a connector-route limitation, not evidence of GitHub permission denial. No Traffic count is claimed.


### Compact Jobs API step-summary omission guard (2026-11-19)

- A compact `actions/runs/{run_id}/jobs` response can return a job record while omitting its step details. An empty or missing `steps` field in that compact response is not evidence that the job had no checkout.
- After job enumeration, use the dedicated workflow-job-steps endpoint and decoded job logs to establish checkout step number/name/status, action, explicit ref, `fetch-depth`, and the actual post-checkout `git log -1 --format=%H` value. Record which source supports each field.
- If the dedicated step endpoint and job log disagree, preserve UNKNOWN and investigate; do not infer a negative checkout observation from a compact summary.
- Counterexample: the two `Maintain H(s)H navigation` jobs #43747347981 and #43747508618 in the 2026-11-15 18:30-18:39:59Z partition had successful step-2 checkouts (`fetch-depth=0`) despite the compact Jobs API summary omitting their step details. The h917:s2 report's four-checkout count is corrected additively; two missing rows were appended, with no prior ledger row rewritten.


## Run-list snapshot retention and job-fan-out gate | 2026-11-19

A completed run-list query is not a durable job-level work queue unless its complete response, or a lossless compact run index, is retained and independently read back before job fan-out.

Required snapshot fields:

- Repository, exact UTC query interval, endpoint and query parameters, per_page, page numbers, returned counts, total_count, terminal-page result, retrieval timestamp, and SHA-256 for each raw page or the complete response.
- For every returned run: run_id, run_attempt, workflow_id, created_at, head_sha, head_branch, event, status, and conclusion.
- Preserve raw page JSON or a lossless ordered index. Verify the stored bytes and digest before treating the enumeration as a recoverable queue.
- Bind every subsequent Jobs API result to its exact run_id and run_attempt. NO_JOB_RECORD_RETURNED is valid only after that exact job endpoint has actually been queried.

If the original response and complete run-ID index are absent, record RUN_ID_SNAPSHOT_NOT_RETAINED, preserve the partition cursor, and recover the source snapshot if possible. Do not silently repeat an already-completed census query. A replacement query requires explicit, documented authorization and must be distinguished from the original enumeration.

Ten workflows run bibliography/paper extraction, evidence inventory, external-science sampling, audience/podcast analysis and related derived-resource updates. Internal file paths are omitted from this public report, following the repository's stated private-reference boundary.

GitHub API currently reports **8,650 HsH**, **1,092 SAT** and **790 HSH_RESOURCES** workflow-run records. They are *Actions runs*, not full-clone counts, and not necessarily a complete historical inventory of removed/out-of-retention programs.

## Candidate self-generated clone mechanisms

| Process | Concrete evidence / how it might appear | Classify as GitHub Traffic full clone? |
|---|---|---|
| A fresh Codex/cloud/Git client runs actual `git clone` | Fresh repo workspace could resemble external automated traffic; requires run/provisioning log with mechanism and target | **POSSIBLE; not confirmed from these workflows** |
| GitHub Actions `actions/checkout` | Widespread use; some cross-repository and scheduled. May provision a working tree on a machine not belonging to the user's computer | **UNKNOWN whether counted by Traffic. Do not assume.** |
| Sites editor/deployment/hosted build | Website frontend and repo backend have separate publishing systems; provider might download or checkout repository content | **UNKNOWN pending Sites/editor/build provenance** |
| GitHub connector and Contents REST API, GitHub code search | Extensively used by project assistants, including present work | **NOT a Git clone by itself** |
| `git fetch` or `git pull` in existing checkout | Used in safe writer fresh-base publish pattern | **NOT automatically a new full clone** |
| Archive ZIP/raw HTTP/browser access | Viewer and archive web browsing | **NOT demonstrated to be full clone** |
| Issue-publisher Actions | Owner issue triggers checkout, validated write and comment | **Issue/commit doesn't certify full clone** |
| Hourly ChatGPT Revival Relay (5 leases, 19 personas) | Recreates/continues *agent work identities* using archived conversation states | **Different meaning of 'clone'; does NOT itself imply copying repository** |

Existing ground-truth project controls: [clone mechanism standards](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/CLONE_LEDGER_STANDARD.md), [clone event ledger](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/CLONE_LEDGER.jsonl), [historical sample-date forensic audit](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/CLONE_FORENSICS_SAMPLE_DATE_RECON_2026-09-23.md), [revival relay provenance standard](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/REVIVAL_RELAY_THREAD_FIRST_RULE_2026-10-11.md).

The ledger contains **9 reconstructed self-mechanism events: 8 CONFIRMED NOT A FULL CLONE; 1 POSSIBLE FULL CLONE / MECHANISM UNKNOWN; 0 confirmed full clones**. On May 31, 2026, a user-reported ~282 full-clone SAT traffic count and on Sept 7 ~205 HsH clones were not matched by this bounded historical study to known self-clones. This is not evidence that all other hits were necessarily external or malicious. Identifying an operation from a GitHub Analytics full-clone counter requires independently retained mechanism/actor/date evidence. Traffic windows and Actions logs expire.

**Forensically useful next controls:** record actual clone commands or checkout provenance, timestamp/actor, environment ID, runner job and run IDs, provider setup logs and whether traffic would be counted. Correlate each traffic day with Actions runs, Site deployments, Codex workspaces and Git activity. Classify unknown honestly, never subtract inferred clone events or claim unique external identities without evidence.
