| **Mysearch** | Independent, prioritized direct-request fast lane | Scaffold only; not validated or production-ready |

Mersearch 1.0 supports Boolean `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, implicit AND, parentheses, quoted phrases, proximity searches (`NEAR/n`\), field filters such as `author:`, `role:`, `body:`, `math:`, `title:`, `date:`, `name:`, `path:` and `status:`, plus filename/path globs. Its math mode normalizes notation for retrieval; it does **not** establish algebraic equivalence or perform CAS validation. urlMersearch release instructionshttps://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/MERSEARCH_RELEASES.md\.

There is another important limitation: post-October 26 Mersearch bridge runs publish only a manifest and compact receipts. They deliberately withhold exhaustive raw hit inventories. A successful run can therefore establish that a search was executed over specified roots, but a compact receipt cannot establish that we have inspected every matching result.

## A live lane conflict prevents a new Mersearch request

The four lanes are not all free. The current lane-1 request is a November 2 geometry-fidelity job, still marked `requested` in its request file. The worker instructions also identify an occupied lane-2 request, `perceptual-nexus-early-archive-20261120-01`, whose execution and receipt must be checked before reuse. I will not overwrite either request or treat a stale request file as an idle lane.

That matters for this audit: I have not yet completed a new, request-bound three-root Mersearch search. The generic GitHub searches so far are reconnaissance only, not Mersearch results.

## The repositories have deliberately different jobs

The onboarding document identifies three distinct repositories. That division is important for interpreting both the automation and the GitHub statistics.

| Repository | Its intended job | What counts as authoritative there |
|--------|--------|--------|
| `SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25` | Historical SAT preservation, source recovery, genealogy and reconstruction | Original records, source chronology and provenance |
| `HsH` | Live project state, current theory controls, worker coordination, tooling and active work | Current BEDROCK, live directives, workflow state and verified work products |
| `HSH_RESOURCES` | External references, bibliography, extraction, comparison and exposure evidence | Source records, extraction manifests and appropriately reviewed citations |

The old SAT archive is explicitly *sedimentary*\: current formulations, superseded branches, experiments, conversations, audits and tools coexist. Its root README points AI visitors to welcome documents in an `AI` folder, but the likely `AI/README.md`, `AI/START_HERE.md` and `AI/Welcome.md` paths currently return 404. The root README itself is therefore an important welcome surface, and the missing target is a real navigation defect worth recording, not a reason to assume the archive has no further AI guidance.

HsH’s urlthree-repository onboarding guidehttps://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/INSTANCE_ONBOARDING_3REPO.md is unusually explicit about these boundaries. It says to use the historical archive for provenance, HsH for current work, and HSH\_RESOURCES for external evidence. It also warns that a polished summary, an index entry, or a repeated claim is not a substitute for reading the source.

HSH\_RESOURCES’ urlAI start pagehttps://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/indexes/AI_START_HERE.md reinforces the private-reference boundary: that repository should not become a public cross-link target or an accidental source of theory authority. Its extraction manifest is the authoritative map from original source path to content hash to extracted text. Its derived-text directory is content-addressed and its GitHub folder view is truncated beyond 1,000 entries, so a visual directory listing is not a completeness test.

## The GitHub-stat corpus is larger and messier than one folder

The key finding aid is urlHSH\_RESOURCES/EXPOSURE\_STATS/GITHUB\_STATS\_INDEX.mdhttps://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/GITHUB_STATS_INDEX.md\. It is a *discovery index*, not an exhaustive inventory. It points to three families of evidence\:

- **Raw captures\:** CSVs for clones, unique cloners, views, unique visitors and commits; screenshots; OCR extracts; and pasted GitHub Insights pages.
- **Historical and cross-repository records\:** captures in the SAT archive, HsH conversation dumps, dated traffic captures, and the cross-master chronology.
- **Interpretive and forensic material\:** assistant conversations, clone-footprint check-ins, clone ledgers, worker handoffs and workflow-attribution notes.

It also records duplicated exports: a file renamed or copied into another folder is not another observation when its Git blob SHA is identical. And because GitHub Traffic is a rolling 14-day view, snapshots taken at different times must not be added together as though they were non-overlapping periods.

That gives us a useful working rule: **build the chronology from raw captures and their content identities first; use the assistant analyses and worker reports to generate hypotheses, not to supply telemetry.**

# Three-repository automation and GitHub-stat audit

I’ve inspected the live repository structures, the central onboarding and worker-control documents, the search machinery, the clone ledger, representative raw statistics, and the public-site development log. The picture is more complicated than “lots of workers, lots of clones.” The three repositories now form a fairly elaborate operating system, but some of its most important controls are more mature on paper than they are in execution.

The strongest finding is that **Mersearch 1.0 really has been run across all three repositories at substantial scale. Mysearch is not yet a production-ready independent search service.** And the GitHub clone statistics remain only partially attributable, even though the automation footprint is now much better documented.

## 1\. Mysearch and Mersearch: what actually works

### Mersearch 1.0 is the working three-repository search engine

The documented stable engine supports\:

| Capability | Mersearch 1.0 |
|--------|--------|
| Boolean logic | `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, implicit AND, parentheses |
| Phrase search | Quoted phrases |
| Proximity | `NEAR/n` |
| Field filters | `author:`, `role:`, `body:`, `math:`, `title:`, `date:`, `name:`, `path:`, `status:` |
| Path selection | Exact paths and filename/path patterns |
| Math-oriented search | Mathematical notation normalization for retrieval |
| Result ordering | Date-oriented and other documented sorting |
| Output | JSON, Markdown and related machine-readable formats |
| Repository scope | HsH, SAT archive and HSH\_RESOURCES |

One important qualification: math normalization helps locate expressions written in different notational forms. It does not prove mathematical equivalence, perform symbolic algebra, or certify a derivation. That distinction matters when using it to search historical equations.

The most useful proof that the three-repository engine has genuinely executed is the existing request `perceptual-nexus-early-archive-20261120-01`\. Its published manifest and receipt identify the pinned stable engine, all three source commit SHAs, and the search coverage\:

**Verified three-repository Mersearch run**

# 22,755

Files scanned

# 22.83M

Records scanned

# 6,850

Search hits

# 1,181

Distinct source paths

---

**Hits by repository root**

| Repository | Hits |
|--------|--------|
| SAT archive | 2,731 |
| HsH | 3,740 |
| HSH\_RESOURCES | 379 |

Sources: urlrun manifesthttps://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/indexes/mersearch_requests/perceptual-nexus-early-archive-20261120-01/RUN_MANIFEST.json · urlsearch receipthttps://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/indexes/mersearch_requests/perceptual-nexus-early-archive-20261120-01/SEARCH_RECEIPT.md\.

This is important evidence of scale, but there is a limit: the full raw result files were deliberately withheld from the repository. The public receipt is a compact navigation aid, not the full hit inventory. Detailed HSH\_RESOURCES paths and excerpts are redacted. So I can verify that the search ran, its inputs, its broad coverage and its totals, but not independently inspect every hit from that run.

### The lanes need reconciliation, not another request dropped on top

The four Mersearch request lanes are shared mutable request surfaces. The worker instructions explicitly say not to overwrite a live request. I found existing requests in those lanes, including the lane-2 perceptual-nexus request. Its output artifacts exist, even though the request file remains marked `requested`\.

That is a state-reconciliation problem: a request file, Actions run, manifest, receipt and final status should agree. Until they do, a lane should not be treated as free merely because its output appears old.

I did **not** submit a new request or modify any lane during this audit.

### Mysearch is still a scaffold

The separate Mysearch implementation is intended to give direct requests priority over ordinary Mersearch traffic. Its design is sensible: a separate ingress, dedicated concurrency group, immutable request IDs, durable status, recoverable preemption, and the same validated three-repository search engine.

But its own implementation plan labels it\:

(IMPLEMENTATION SCAFFOLD / NOT YET DEPLOYED OR VALIDATED)

I confirmed the workflow source exists, but the expected `indexes/mysearch_requests/` output directory is absent. The implementation plan also records the following blockers\:

- It has no durable pre-runner queue or true immediate acknowledgement. Its initial acknowledgement happens after a runner starts.
- Its concurrency setting limits simultaneous work but does not provide a persistent request queue.
- Its checkout evidence records repository names and HEAD SHAs, but not the complete run/job/step/ref/depth/environment identity needed for the canonical ledger.
- Checkout evidence is written to a temporary file and is not appended to the clone ledger.
- Its recorded completion time is created during manifest preparation, before publication and independent readback are complete.

This is not a cosmetic distinction. **A workflow file that can be manually dispatched is not the same thing as an operational service with durable intake, queue state, recovery and verified delivery.**

There is also an important boundary between the public `CONVERSATION_VIEWER/mersearch/` page and research Mersearch. The public reader is a candidate search over a curation-approved conversation index. Its own development log says it is *not* the pinned, three-repository Mersearch engine with `NEAR` and math normalization. It should not be mistaken for full archive access.

Relevant controls: urlMysearch implementation planhttps://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/MYSEARCH_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md · urlMersearch release noteshttps://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/MERSEARCH_RELEASES.md · urlMersearch worker start guidehttps://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/MERSEARCH_WORKER_START_HERE.md\.

## 2\. Automation across all three repositories

The automation is not concentrated in one central workflow. Each repository has its own machinery, which is consistent with the different roles assigned to them.

**HsH** (Live coordination and tooling)

# 40

Entries in `.github/workflows/`

Covers navigation maintenance, conversation tagging and indexing, viewer generation, public-site discovery, issue publication, Mersearch bridges, Mysearch prototype, math extraction, provenance audits, paper publication and other maintenance operations.

---

**HSH\_RESOURCES** (Research infrastructure)

# 10

Workflow files

Covers source inventory, bibliography coverage, paper extraction, cross-archive cataloguing, audience metrics, podcast indexing and focused cross-diffusion/OCR data compilation.

---

**SAT\_THEORY\_ARCHIVE\_2023-25** (Historical archive machinery)

# 10

Actionable workflow YAML files in a 13-entry workflow directory

Covers full-archive indexing, Archive Admin, PDF extraction, SAT-mention tagging, folder indexing and the Floating Liars’ Club digitization/story-feed work. The older archive-structure builder is explicitly marked legacy/disabled.

The workflow directory counts above are file counts, not successful run counts.

### What the automation actually does

**HsH is the control plane.** Its recurring maintenance processes include the automatic website discovery docket, navigation and date-tagging, conversation viewer generation, archive-wide chronology and autotag indexes, cross-source integrity checks and publication intake. The large `maintain-navigation.yml` workflow is particularly consequential: it performs a chain of repository maintenance steps, validates Python and JavaScript, runs tests, generates navigation, and deploys the conversation viewer through Pages.

**HSH\_RESOURCES is the evidence and extraction engine.** Its `source-inventory.yml` workflow actually checks out all three repositories, records their source revisions, then runs a quarantine-respecting inventory process. Its paper-extraction and bibliography-coverage workflows generate derived text, indexes, straggler queues and human-review intake. Its cross-diffusion workflow combines focused PDF extraction, OCR and structured analytics.

**The SAT archive has its own preservation and reconstruction loop.** `full-archive-index.yml` maintains its structural index. `archive-admin.yml` handles archive maintenance and selected extraction tasks. `extract-pdf-text.yml` provides a focused extraction path. The old structural builder remains disabled, rather than being silently treated as current infrastructure.

That separation is valuable. It prevents the historical archive from becoming a mutable copy of the current project, and prevents the external-reference repository from becoming a substitute for the source archive.

### The cross-repository search bridge is itself a major automation source

A Mersearch bridge run checks out four repositories: HsH, the stable Mersearch branch, the SAT archive and HSH\_RESOURCES. It uses a full-history checkout for HsH and shallow checkouts for the others, then runs the same pinned search engine against the three source repositories.

The three-repository math-hopper pilot also performs shallow checkouts of all three repositories. HSH\_RESOURCES’ inventory workflow checks out its own repository with full history and the other two shallowly.

This means that a single logical research operation can involve several repository materializations. Counting workflow runs alone would understate the number of checkout operations, while counting every repository event as a separate human clone would overstate what we know about people.

### The current scheduler is a separate layer

The active automation roster still describes five fixed hourly relay IDs, with a 19-identity rotation. A later scheduler readback in that document supersedes the earlier five-enabled statement: four tasks were enabled, and the existing `:12` task was disabled. Its original schedule remained present; the reason for disablement was not established.

The roster explicitly says not to re-enable that task without authorization and not to create a sixth recurrence. The worker rotation therefore needs to be understood as identities being selected by the existing scheduler machinery, not as nineteen separate enabled scheduled tasks.

This matters for interpreting worker reports. A scheduled recurrence, a selected identity, a successful execution and a verified historical conversation re-entry are four different things.

Relevant reading: urlactive automation rosterhttps://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/ACTIVE_AUTOMATION_ROSTER.md · urlautomation and workflow controlhttps://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/AUTOMATION_WORKFLOW_CONTROL.md · urlworkflow branching maphttps://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/WORKFLOW_BRANCHING_MAP.md\.

## 3\. Welcome pages and AI-facing surfaces

The three-repository onboarding system is quite explicit about repository roles\:

| Repository | AI/worker orientation |
|--------|--------|
| SAT archive | Historical source, chronology, provenance and reconstruction |
| HsH | Current directives, shared work state, branch routing, worker coordination and tooling |
| HSH\_RESOURCES | External references, source extraction, bibliography, benchmarks and exposure evidence |

The HsH onboarding guide is the strongest single cross-repository entry point. It tells a new instance to read current control state rather than blindly inherit an old worker's summaries. The archive's root README similarly presents the archive as a historical record, not a current authority source.

HSH\_RESOURCES has a dedicated AI start page. Its source and extraction instructions distinguish original records from derived text, and its index explains that the extraction manifest maps source paths to content identities. This is important because a very large folder can have several copies of a source under different filenames.

### Navigation defects and visibility boundaries

I found two things worth flagging.

First, the SAT archive's root README directs AI visitors toward AI-specific welcome material, but the obvious guessed paths for `AI/README.md`, `AI/START_HERE.md` and `AI/Welcome.md` did not resolve. The archive's actual access guide and root README remain available, so this does not invalidate its onboarding. It does suggest that the precise AI entry route needs to be checked against the real directory tree and repaired if the references are stale.

Second, HSH\_RESOURCES has a documented reference-private role, while prior repository operations reports flag that GitHub's repository visibility metadata has shown it as public. The repository should not be treated as private merely because its README says it is for internal reference. That discrepancy deserves an owner-side GitHub settings check. The resources repository's own instructions also prohibit casually syndicating its contents into public-facing pages.

### Public site and AI-facing search

The HsH development log is unusually candid about the distinction between repository source changes and successful publication. A successful GitHub commit or Pages workflow does not by itself prove that the intended public route displays the right content.

The log records a November 1–2 attempt to rebuild the site after the ChatGPT Sites editor became unavailable, a successful GitHub Pages deployment, and then a corrective rollback after the initial rebuild exceeded the intended scope. The subsequent direction narrowed the effort to preserving the original Conversation Viewer and publishing the Whirligig route without replacing the whole site.

The site documentation also requires a default-deny presentation contract: raw machine JSON, unpresented Markdown/TeX, staging assets and control files should not fall through into ordinary reader pages. A reader should receive an audience-appropriate document or an explicit pending state.

That is the right architecture. The remaining risk is keeping the source, feed, renderer, deployed build and live route synchronized. The log itself says those are separate verification stages.

Sources: urlthree-repository onboardinghttps://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/INSTANCE_ONBOARDING_3REPO.md · urlHSH\_RESOURCES AI start pagehttps://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/indexes/AI_START_HERE.md · urlSAT archive READMEhttps://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/README.md · urlpublic-site work loghttps://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/PUBLIC_SITE/SITE_DEVELOPMENT_WORK_LOG.md\.

## 4\. Worker-facing documentation and recommendations

The central workflow architecture is more sophisticated than a task list. It explicitly models work as a branching system with entry conditions, dependencies, evidence requirements, handoffs, exit criteria, return triggers and retirement or supersession states.

The urlWorkflow Leverage / Signal-Switch Protocolhttps://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/WORKFLOW_LEVERAGE_SIGNAL_PROTOCOL.md is particularly important. It tells the Comptroller to inspect the work system itself for\:

- **Starved branches\:** useful work repeatedly bypassed.
- **Entrenched methods\:** the same worker or method repeated without adding information.
- **Orphaned outputs\:** artifacts with no consumer or return route.
- **Recommendation debt\:** actionable recommendations with no disposition.
- **Feed stalls\:** work produced upstream but never consumed downstream.
- **Incorporation failures\:** machinery exists, but workers are not discovering or using it.

A recommendation should eventually become `ACCEPTED / ROUTED`, `TESTED`, `BRANCHED`, `NIBBLED`, `PARKED + RETURN TRIGGER`, `REJECTED + REASON`, `DUPLICATE / MERGED` or `NEEDS NATHAN`\. This is a practical design for turning discussion into decisions and decisions into work.

The urlAutomation Workflow Controlhttps://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/AUTOMATION_WORKFLOW_CONTROL.md adds an execution loop: AIM, RECON, EXECUTE, VERIFY, RETURN. It tells workers to investigate existing tools and external capabilities before building replacements, use Mersearch for archive discovery, and distinguish a proposed solution from a tested or deployed one.

It also imposes adoption tests. For example, the 19-identity rotation is not considered successful merely because the scheduler selects names. Receipts should demonstrate actual identity selection, substantive work, protected specialist remits, lateral reading, tool experiments and meaningful handoffs. The Orson cognition remit is specifically protected, with a target of four out of five substantive turns serving that work.

### The gap between the recommendation system and its adoption

The documentation repeatedly warns that the presence of a control is not proof of its use. That is correct, and the work logs show why.

The November 3 clone-footprint census records 19/19 ring-label dispositions, but 17 were reconstructed and two unavailable. It reports zero authenticated first-hand current-thread worker responses. This is an important limitation: reconstructed reports are useful evidence, but they are not the same as a worker directly confirming what it did.

Likewise, the roster says the scheduler configuration was changed and verified, but explicitly says that configuration does not establish that subsequent workers followed the instructions.

The work system has the right conceptual tests. The next challenge is making their measurements automatic and routine rather than periodically reconstructing them from a pile of receipts.

## 5\. What the GitHub-stat archive actually tells us

The primary finding aid is urlHSH\_RESOURCES/EXPOSURE\_STATS/GITHUB\_STATS\_INDEX.mdhttps://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/GITHUB_STATS_INDEX.md\. It points to the central `EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT  Satobloc GitHubStats/` collection, SAT-era captures, HsH conversation dumps, root-level text captures, and screenshot/OCR derivatives.

Its own warning is essential: the inventory is an initial discovery pass, not exhaustive. It directs later workers to enumerate every CSV, text capture, screenshot and OCR derivative, compare source hashes, preserve attribution uncertainty, and avoid adding overlapping rolling windows.

### Verified historical snapshots

A few captures have explicit repository identity and can be reported directly\:

| Repository / capture | Clones | Unique cloners | Views | Unique visitors |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| HsH, September 15–22, 2026 | 11,912 | 1,735 | 1,295 | 2 |
| SAT archive, August 26 snapshot | 579 | 509 | 26 | 3 |
| SAT archive, August 28–September 4 snapshot | 26 | 13 | 180 | 15 |

The HsH capture is `HSH_TRAFFIC_23SEP26.txt`; the two SAT captures are `GITHUB_8-26_STATS.txt` in the archive and `PRE_HSH_ROUNDUP/github rep.txt`\. These are separate historical observations, not current live telemetry.

The HsH numbers are especially striking: 11,912 clones but only two unique visitors. That is consistent with a large amount of non-browser or programmatic repository activity. It is not proof that all that activity was yours, ChatGPT's, GitHub Actions, or anyone else.

There are also large later-looking values in the collection. The `58k.JPG` OCR extract reports 58,677 HsH clones, 5,897 unique cloners and one unique visitor. Its capture date remains unestablished. The associated index explicitly says to correlate the screenshot with contemporaneous records before assigning a date. It should not be treated as a fresh current reading.

### The CSV series and text captures need reconciliation

The HSH\_RESOURCES corpus contains numerous CSV exports for clones, unique cloners, views, unique visitors, commits and code frequency. Some numbered or renamed copies have identical Git blob SHAs. Those are duplicate files, not independent datasets.

The HsH-era CSV series associated with the October 24–November 6 period shows daily clone counts rising into the thousands, with daily unique-cloner counts also rising. Its accompanying view and visitor series remain very small by comparison. That supports the interpretation that ordinary page browsing is not explaining most of the cloning activity.

But there is a data hygiene issue: filenames and folder placement are not sufficient to establish the repository identity of every CSV. The index's own attribution rules say to use explicit labels first and mark inferred assignments as inferred. Some text captures also combine multiple GitHub Insights panels or multiple snapshots. They need to be separated by capture identity before any aggregation.

The urlcross-master chronologyhttps://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/CROSS_MASTER_CHRONOLOGY.md contains dated series, but it deliberately preserves conflicting or overlapping records rather than reconciling them into one definitive timeline. That is preferable to silently choosing whichever file agrees with a favored interpretation.

## 6\. Clone accounting: the most important correction

The current urlclone ledger standardhttps://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/CLONE_LEDGER_STANDARD.md makes a distinction that should govern all future analysis\:

1. **Checkout materialization\:** did a workflow create a working copy, and was it shallow or full-history?
2. **Traffic attribution\:** did GitHub actually count that operation in its Traffic clone statistics?

These are different questions. The standard explicitly says only an authorized GitHub Traffic observation can resolve the second one.

I parsed the current `CLONE_LEDGER.jsonl`\:

**Current clone ledger**

# 527

JSONL records, zero parse errors

| Classification | Records |
|--------|--------|
| Confirmed not a full clone | 257 |
| Checkout materialization known, Traffic unknown | 169 |
| Other possible, incomplete or unknown classifications | 101 |

---

**Repository distribution**

| Repository | Records |
|--------|--------|
| HsH | 337 |
| SAT archive | 109 |
| HSH\_RESOURCES | 76 |
| Other repositories | 5 |

These are ledger records, not unique clone events. Some entries are supplements or corrections, and one logical operation can produce multiple records across repositories.

The Traffic-attribution field has\:

- 402 `UNKNOWN`
- 100 `NO`
- 25 unspecified

The 169 materialized-checkout records are therefore **not 169 verified GitHub Traffic clones**\. They are known runner checkouts whose Traffic attribution remains unresolved.

This also corrects my earlier simplification that a successful `actions/checkout` could be counted as a Traffic clone. An external controlled experiment found a one-to-one relationship in its test setup, but the HsH ledger's formal evidentiary standard deliberately does not adopt that as an observation. The ledger's stricter rule should govern the project.

### What this means for the percentage question

We can now estimate the size of the project's internal *checkout activity* much better than before. We cannot yet determine what percentage of the actual Traffic clone total was caused by your own activity.

The missing bridge is a matched dataset connecting\:

- the daily GitHub Traffic clone and unique-cloner observations;
- Actions run, job and checkout-step identities across all three repositories;
- other automated and hosted repository provisioning;
- your local scripts and device-based Git activity;
- ChatGPT-initiated operations and their actual execution environments.

A unique cloner is not a person, ChatGPT conversation, worker identity or commit author. Without source-level attribution, the numbers cannot distinguish your own hosted automation from unrelated automation.

## 7\. The main architectural findings

Here is where I think the next improvements have the highest leverage.

| Status | Finding | Why it matters |
|--------|--------|--------|
| (Working) | Mersearch 1.0 has verified three-repository execution | Real full-corpus discovery is possible |
| (Incomplete) | Mysearch is not production-ready | Direct requests still lack durable queue and completion guarantees |
| (Reconcile) | Mersearch request files and published receipts can disagree | Lanes may remain apparently occupied after completed work |
| (Incomplete) | GitHub-stat index is not exhaustive | The traffic chronology is still incomplete |
| (Unknown) | Actions checkout to Traffic attribution | Internal activity cannot yet be converted to observed Traffic counts |
| (Adoption test) | Worker instructions exceed demonstrated first-hand adoption | The machinery may be more mature than its execution evidence |
| (Navigation repair) | SAT archive AI welcome references need checking | New workers may miss their intended entry route |
| (Visibility check) | HSH\_RESOURCES visibility and reference-private documentation conflict | Risk of unintended exposure or incorrect assumptions about access |

### My recommended order

**First: finish the Mysearch machinery.** It is the biggest capability multiplier. Give it a durable request/event store, immediate acknowledgement before runner allocation, safe recovery and preemption, complete checkout identities, and a real end-to-end acceptance test. The search engine is already there. The missing work is the service architecture around it.

**Second: complete the GitHub-stat census.** The existing finding aid already defines the method. Build one deduplicated capture registry from all three repositories, including root-level and nested `.csv` and `.txt` files, screenshots, OCR extracts, and text embedded in conversation dumps. Each observation should have repository identity, capture timestamp/window, metric, content hash, source type, attribution confidence and duplicate-family ID. Preserve competing records rather than forcing premature agreement.

**Third: reconcile the Mersearch lanes.** Match every mutable request file to its Actions run, manifest, receipt, publication commit and independently read-back output. Mark completed requests complete and release their lanes only after that evidence agrees. Do not merely clear old-looking request files.

**Fourth: make the worker adoption test machine-readable.** The existing workflow leverage protocol already specifies the right signals. A small event schema could capture recommendation ID, origin, disposition, owner, pickup run, artifact, evidence, and return trigger. Then recommendation debt and actual uptake become calculable rather than inferred from reports.

**Fifth: repair the welcome and access routes.** Validate all AI-facing links in the three repositories, especially the SAT archive's welcome references, and resolve the HSH\_RESOURCES visibility discrepancy. Make the initial worker path point to one current three-repository orientation, followed by repository-specific rules.

---

## Bottom line

The repos already contain much of the architecture needed for a genuinely capable, self-maintaining research workspace. The most valuable pieces are the three-repository division of responsibility, stable Mersearch, the workflow branching model, the recommendation disposition protocol, and the explicit separation of materialization from Traffic attribution.

The weak point is not a shortage of machinery. It is **the gap between machinery, adoption, and independently verifiable outcomes**\.

The highest-leverage next step is to turn Mysearch into the durable three-repository ingress and make its provenance pipeline the model for the rest of the automation. That would simultaneously improve research access, worker continuity, source attribution, and the ability to calculate what the automation is actually doing.

I have only read and audited the repository state in this pass. I did not change files, submit search requests, alter scheduler tasks or modify any workflow.

## GitHub connector route: parallel request lanes

**Updated 2026-10-24:** the former single-slot bridge has been expanded to **four independent request lanes**. All lanes run the same pinned `mersearch-stable-1.0` searcher over the same three permitted roots and publish request-scoped outputs into `indexes/mersearch_requests/<request_id>/`.

Available request files:
- Lane 1 / legacy: `WORKSPACES/COMMON/MERSEARCH_REQUEST.json`
- Lane 2: `WORKSPACES/COMMON/MERSEARCH_REQUEST_LANE_2.json`
- Lane 3: `WORKSPACES/COMMON/MERSEARCH_REQUEST_LANE_3.json`
- Lane 4: `WORKSPACES/COMMON/MERSEARCH_REQUEST_LANE_4.json`

Each lane has its own GitHub Actions workflow and its own concurrency group, so searches on different lanes can run in parallel subject to the repository/account's available GitHub Actions runner concurrency.

**Do not duplicate the Mersearch code itself just to gain throughput.** The bottleneck was the single request file plus single workflow concurrency group, not the search implementation. Keep one pinned implementation and multiply the bridge lanes.

1. Inspect the lane request files and choose an idle lane. **Do not overwrite** a lane whose request is still pending/running or whose output has not been verified. If all lanes are occupied, use a local pinned Mersearch checkout or wait/coordinate rather than overwriting another worker's request. Do not pretend connector code search is a Mersearch result.
2. When a lane is free, write a fresh globally unique `request_id`, a query using the stable 1.0 language, requester and purpose into that lane's request file. A change to the lane file on `main` starts that lane's workflow.
3. Retrieve the request-scoped folder `indexes/mersearch_requests/<request_id>/` and verify `RUN_MANIFEST.json`, `SEARCH_RECEIPT.json` and `SEARCH_RECEIPT.md`. **For post-2026-10-26 containment runs, these are the only three files intentionally published by the bridge**; do not treat absent `SEARCH_RESULTS.json/.md` as a failed run or claim that compact receipts contain all hits.    - **Historical pre-containment runs** may also have public `SEARCH_RESULTS.json` and `SEARCH_RESULTS.md`. Their existence is not authorization to redistribute raw excerpts; assess exposure before reuse. For complete post-containment results, execute pinned Mersearch against an authorized local three-root checkout or use an approved restricted durable artifact route. `RUN_MANIFEST.json` may contain digests for raw outputs generated inside the job even though those outputs were **not** published. 4. Confirm the **actual** searched repositories, exact source SHAs, stable Mersearch implementation ref, exclusions and completion. Failed or incomplete runs are not results. Remember: scan exclusions and large files may limit completeness even if three repositories were checked out.

## Execution-to-artifact binding

A request ID and compact manifest do not, by themselves, identify the execution attempt that produced the artifacts. For every bridge run, preserve the chain:

1. Request file path, request ID, requester, query hash and request-file blob SHA.
2. GitHub Actions run ID, run attempt, workflow ID/name, run event, head branch/SHA and status/conclusion.
3. Job ID and each checkout step number/name/status, with the actual repository, ref mode, fetch depth and post-checkout commit SHA.
4. Stable implementation ref/hash **and** any runtime-only patch/hash, kept distinct.
5. Output artifact paths, SHA-256 digests, publication policy, and independent readback of each durable artifact.

If the compact manifest omits run/attempt/job/step identifiers, recover them from the Actions run and job logs and append one clone-ledger row per actual checkout event. Do not infer checkout count from repository count, compare a cross-repository checkout SHA with the HsH workflow head, or treat a successful run as proof of exhaustive search. Raw search-result artifacts remain withheld under the post-containment policy.

From a stable checkout with sibling archive directories visible (paths here are examples):

## Purpose

Build a separately addressable Mysearch ingress and execution path for direct Nathan requests, independent of the four mutable Mersearch compatibility lanes. Keep stable Mersearch 1.0 and its three-repository search semantics as the initial engine. Do not promote or silently substitute the 1.1 index prototype until its multi-repository, profile-isolation, result-parity, concurrency, and latency gates pass.

## Non-negotiable behavior

1. **Priority:** Direct Nathan submissions enter Mysearch and are not placed behind ordinary Mersearch work. The service may interrupt or displace lower-priority Mysearch work if Nathan explicitly invokes it; displaced requests must not be silently lost.
2. **Preemption and collision policy:** Nathan has authorized priority even where disruption occurs. Mysearch may interrupt active work when a direct Nathan request arrives. Before enabling destructive cancellation, the implementation must preserve the active request's logs, run metadata, temporary outputs, and exact last-known stage whenever feasible. If safe checkpointing is unavailable, the status must record the interruption and the request must remain recoverable/re-runnable; cleanup is an explicit recovery action, not hidden data loss.
3. **Isolation:** A separate workflow file, request ingress path, and concurrency group. One active fast-lane search initially. Ordinary Mersearch lanes cannot occupy this slot.
4. **Engine parity:** Stable 1.0, pinned ref `mersearch-stable-1.0`, initially; all three permitted repositories remain in scope: HsH, SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25, and HSH_RESOURCES. Preserve existing exclusions, privacy boundaries, query semantics, provenance, source commit SHAs and compact receipt rules.
5. **Immediate acknowledgement:** Every submission gets an immutable request ID and a status receipt before runner allocation. Expose state, queue position (or explicit active/runner-wait status), timestamp of acceptance, observed_at, and each blocking request's submitted_at and last_transition_at. Store canonical UTC; render all Nathan-facing times in America/New_York (ET).
6. **No false status:** Distinguish runner wait, checkout/materialization, search, packaging, publishing, complete, failed, cancelled, preempted, and recovery-needed. COMPLETE requires durable manifest and receipt readback plus checksum agreement.
7. **Overflow:** Explicit route to ordinary Mersearch lanes only with a user-visible overflow disposition. Never label overflow as Mysearch execution.
8. **No silent pending loss:** Immutable request records and append-only event history. Mutable request files may be compatibility adapters only.

## Clone-observability specification (required by BEDROCK ND-2026-11-20-01)

This process accesses/provisions repository-bearing environments in HsH, Glass (SAT archive), HSH_RESOURCES, and the stable Mersearch runtime checkout. Every checkout step must emit a deduplicated event containing repository, workflow/run/attempt/job/step, action/ref/depth, checkout SHA where available, timestamp precision, and environment identity. At run end publish per-repository confirmed checkout/materialization counts, possible/unknown events, confirmed non-clone operations, and Traffic attribution state. Checkout events must not be represented as observed GitHub Traffic clones. Traffic clone and unique-cloner observations are separate repository/window snapshots and must be reported only when actually retrieved. Append to the existing clone ledger or its approved publisher path; do not create a competing ledger. Missing telemetry is UNKNOWN, never zero.

## Implementation sequence

### M0: Isolated ingress and single-flight runner
- Add a Mysearch request schema and dedicated workflow on explicit dispatch / request event.
- Generate immutable request IDs, query digest, timestamps, request state and per-request output directory.
- Use a dedicated concurrency group with one active slot.
- For the first safe release, avoid automatic cancellation of an active request. Implement the event/receipt/preemption metadata first; turn on Nathan-authorized disruptive preemption only after a checkpoint/recovery test demonstrates that request state and outputs survive interruption.
- Build a status and receipt artifact from the run itself. Add durable append-only event history. A single mutable JSON file is not a multi-writer queue.
- Reject or explicitly supersede duplicate request IDs; never overwrite a different live request.

### M1: Result publication and source verification
- Reuse the stable 1.0 search script and the bridge's bounded compact receipt publisher.
- Retain raw result files only in the permitted job workspace; do not publish raw excerpts or private HSH_RESOURCES material.
- Include the three source repository commit SHAs, engine ref/commit, script/runtime digests, query digest, exclusions, result totals, exact output digests, and publication/readback verification.
- Include a final status path and queue/timing receipt; preserve UTC timestamps and ET rendering metadata.

### M2: Central lifecycle queue and fair displaced-work handling
- Replace mutable lane files as authoritative state with an append-only event store and transactional/compare-and-swap transitions.
- Support SUBMITTED, QUEUED, CLAIMED, RUNNING, PACKAGING, PUBLISHING, COMPLETE, FAILED, CANCELLED, PREEMPTED, RECOVERY_NEEDED and EXPIRED.
- On Nathan's direct invocation, assign priority immediately; active lower-priority work may be preempted as authorized, with a recoverable tombstone and displaced-work requeue record. Preserve original submission time and attempt lineage.
- Queue receipts include per-request submission and transition timestamps for every request ahead, class position, global scheduling context, observed_at, and timezone.
- Do not claim a completion-time estimate until measured latency distributions exist.

### M3: Indexed engine promotion gate
- Extend 1.1 immutable SQLite/FTS from HsH-only to all three allowed repositories and explicit access-controlled corpus profiles.
- Validate source commit provenance, exclusions at build and query time, result parity against stable 1.0, complete result totals, eight mixed readers including the interactive lane during rebuild, old-generation availability, failure retention, and real-corpus p50/p95 latency.
- No primary traffic cutover before all gates pass.

## Acceptance tests

- A direct Nathan request receives an ID, acceptance timestamp and status before a runner starts.
- Fast lane runs independently of all four ordinary bridge lanes.
- Ordinary submissions cannot displace a direct Nathan request.
- A direct Nathan request can preempt active lower-priority Mysearch work only after a recovery record is durably written; if interrupted, displaced work has a visible recoverable state and attempt lineage.
- One active fast-lane request maximum; overflow is explicit.
- Queue timestamps are correct, UTC canonical, America/New_York rendered for Nathan, and stable across retries and reprioritization.
- Three-repository coverage, exclusions, source SHAs and result parity are verified.
- Each repository checkout is counted once per run/attempt/job/step; API/file fetches are not inflated into clones; Traffic attribution remains UNKNOWN without a Traffic observation.
- COMPLETE requires independently readable receipt and manifest with digest agreement.

## Current blockers and known state

- Four standard Mersearch request lanes exist and are occupied; lane 2 contains request `perceptual-nexus-early-archive-20261120-01`. Do not overwrite or reuse it.

- No durable central queue/status ledger is deployed.
- This plan does not modify existing Mersearch lane files, stable engine refs, shared scheduler tasks or unrelated workflows.

## Definition of done

Mysearch is operational only when a Nathan Direct request can be submitted into the independent ingress, gets an immediate durable status/queue receipt, runs the same validated three-repository search with auditable provenance, reports clone/materialization/Traffic/unique-cloner quantities separately, and returns a result whose manifest and compact receipt pass independent readback. Until then its state must be reported as scaffold, prototype, or blocked, never deployed.

- a clearly identified **summary/paraphrase** with source citation/provenance;
- for private/raw project data, an appropriate **public-safe extract or summary** stating what was analyzed and its provenance.

Internal ledgers/research notes may retain an HSH_RESOURCES repository-relative path and content hash so the exact archived copy can be recovered. That private locator is not itself the public citation.

Private source repository for scientific papers, raw datasets, and their derived navigation artifacts used during the H(s)H reconstruction.

This repository is evidence storage, not the public synthesis. A paper's presence here does not endorse it, make it relevant, or establish an H(s)H claim. Public synthesis statements belong in [`Satobloc/HsH`](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH) and should cite the original external source supporting the statement; internal citation handoffs may additionally record the exact resource copy used here.

## Start here

For people browsing the repository, use [`!_HSH_RESOURCES_INDEX.md`](!%5FHSH%5FRESOURCES%5FINDEX.md). It consolidates reviewed and provisional source records into one navigable catalog with title, author/metadata, identifier/date, source type, review/read status, exact repository path, and a concise description or identity note.

For Janus and other H(s)H agents, use [`indexes/AI_START_HERE.md`](indexes/AI_START_HERE.md). It routes directly into the two priority technical corridors—`PRIOR_ART` and `H(s)H_Toolkit`—and specifies how to move from bounded catalog records to the structural index, extraction manifest, and extracted full text without treating external literature as H(s)H theory authority.

Supporting layers remain separate:

- `indexes/AI_START_HERE.md` — compact AI/LLM routing contract and priority-corridor entry point.
- `indexes/ai_source_index/` — focused AI corridors for `PRIOR_ART` and `H(s)H_Toolkit`.
- `indexes/HUMAN_BIBLIOGRAPHY.md` — reviewed bibliography policy, PRIOR_ART notes, and citation handoffs.
- `indexes/bibliography_batches/` — bounded human/LLM-reviewed bibliography batches.
- `indexes/bibliography_provisional/` — bounded machine-generated identity/navigation batches for successfully extracted sources.
- `indexes/BIBLIOGRAPHY_COVERAGE.md` — machine coverage accounting.
- `indexes/BIBLIOGRAPHY_STRAGGLERS.md` — unresolved extraction/indexing exceptions.
- `indexes/RESOURCE_INDEX.md` and `indexes/index-state.json` — structural machine inventory.

## Theorybuilding boundary

SAT/H(s)H research and development is reconstructed from the project's own Fundamental Intuitions and internal SAT → SAT-O → 4DHH → Blockwave/Satobloc → H(s)H development. External literature is stored here for bibliographic credit, standard mathematical/physical context, empirical evidence and constraints, prior-art comparison, and explicitly provenance-labeled imports. Related outside theories are not silently treated as the generative basis of H(s)H.

The source-side citation and handoff surface is `indexes/HUMAN_BIBLIOGRAPHY.md`. The receiving point-of-use ledger in the public theory repository is `Satobloc/HsH/ledgers/CITATION_LEDGER.md`. When an actual citation need is identified, record the same stable `CITE-YYYY-NNN` handoff ID on both sides with the exact source and theory destination. The HSH_RESOURCES side may store the private archived-copy path/hash; the public HsH side should expose the bibliographic citation/source rather than the private repo link.

## Repository layers

- `HAUL */` and other source folders — uploaded source material; preserve files as received.
- `tools/` — deterministic extraction, indexing, bibliography, and coverage utilities.
- `indexes/RESOURCE_INDEX.md` — generated structural catalog.
- `indexes/index-state.json` — machine-readable structural scan state.
- `indexes/HUMAN_BIBLIOGRAPHY.md` — reviewed bibliography and source-side citation handoffs.
- `indexes/BIBLIOGRAPHY_COVERAGE.md` — generated reviewed/provisional/exclusion accounting.
- `derived/text/` — page-marked text extraction keyed by source-content SHA-256; not a source inventory.
- `derived/manifests/` — authoritative extraction mapping/results, errors, and OCR-needed status.
- `derived/README.md` — wayfinding for the derived layer and large-directory/truncation warning.

## Large derived-text directory warning

Do not use the GitHub web listing of `derived/text/` as a completeness check. GitHub truncates large directory views at 1,000 entries. The extracted-text count also need not equal the source-PDF count because byte-identical source PDFs share one content-addressed `<sha256>.txt` extraction while retaining separate source-path records.

For complete extraction coverage, use `derived/manifests/extraction.jsonl` as the authoritative `source_path → sha256 → text_path` mapping. The bibliography workflow reads that manifest and corresponding text files from a full checkout; it does not depend on GitHub's truncated directory rendering.

Do not silently rename, deduplicate, repair, or replace source files. Duplicate paths are recorded in the index and can remain as provenance evidence.

## Automated maintenance

The `Extract and index papers` workflow handles new or changed PDFs, extraction, and structural indexing. The `Maintain bibliography coverage` workflow builds provisional bibliography batches, coverage accounting, the human-review intake queue, straggler accounting, and the root human-readable source index.

The presentation layers never promote machine metadata to reviewed status and never infer H(s)H relevance, citation need, prior art, novelty, theoretical authority, or scientific validity.

## Evidence discipline

Keep these judgments separate:

1. the file is present;
2. text was extracted successfully;
3. bibliographic metadata was identified;
4. the source was read;
5. a result is relevant to an H(s)H dependency;
6. an actual citation is needed at a specific HsH point of use;
7. the result supports, conflicts with, constrains, predates, or merely resembles a model construction.

[L2]   "content": "# SAT/H(s)H Clone Ledger

Status: ACTIVE STANDING PROVENANCE CONTROL
Effective: 2026-09-23
Owner: project-wide; any instance/system learning of repository provisioning should append or revise evidence.

## Principle
Record repository-copy/provisioning events even when the mechanism is unknown. Repository presence does not imply a clone. API/connector access, fetch, pull, actions/checkout, archive download, and browser access are not full clones unless evidence establishes GitHub Traffic would count them as such.

## Required classifications
- CONFIRMED FULL CLONE
- CONFIRMED NOT A FULL CLONE
- POSSIBLE FULL CLONE — MECHANISM UNKNOWN
- REPOSITORY PRESENT — PROVISIONING UNKNOWN
- NO EVIDENCE OF REPOSITORY ACCESS

## Required fields
event_id, timestamp, timestamp_precision, actor_system, repository, environment_id, operation, mechanism, fresh_environment, traffic_clone_expected, classification, evidence, purpose, related_id, confidence, prior_classification, revision_reason.

Mechanism vocabulary: git clone; shallow clone; fetch; pull; actions/checkout; API/connector; archive download; cached workspace; unknown provisioning; other.

traffic_clone_expected: YES / NO / UNKNOWN.
fresh_environment: YES / NO / UNKNOWN.

## Revision rule
Never erase an earlier UNKNOWN classification. When later evidence resolves an event, preserve prior_classification and revision_reason.

## Retention
This ledger is provenance infrastructure and is not disposable run-log material. Before shorter-lived operational logs expire, retain identifiers, timestamps, mechanism classification, evidentiary summary, and retained-artifact pointers here.

## Aggregation
Aggregate by repository, UTC/local date as appropriate, actor/system, confirmed full clones, possible full clones, confirmed non-clone access, and unknown provisioning events.

## Fresh cloud/Codex rule
If a fresh Codex/cloud workspace is encountered with the repository already present but provisioning mechanism is not evidenced, record REPOSITORY PRESENT — PROVISIONING UNKNOWN. Do not infer git clone.


## Actions API enumeration and checkout-materialization axes (2026-11-15)

### Run-list completeness

- Query the repository Actions run-list route with an explicit UTC `created` interval, `per_page=100`, and page number. Preserve the exact query, page number, returned count, `total_count`, and terminal-page result.
- Treat `total_count=2500` as cap-saturated and incomplete, not as an exact census. If a daily interval still returns 2500, subdivide into non-overlapping UTC hourly intervals or smaller. For each subinterval, paginate until an empty page and verify that the sum of returned page counts equals the reported count and that run IDs are unique. Use adjacent intervals with explicit boundaries; deduplicate by run ID at any inclusive boundary.
- A run with an empty Jobs API array is `NO_JOB_RECORD_RETURNED`; it is not proof that no checkout occurred. Preserve the run record and do not invent a checkout event.
- For each run, preserve `run_id`, `run_attempt`, `workflow_id`, `head_branch`, `head_sha`, `created_at`, `status`, and `conclusion`. For each job, preserve `job_id`, job status/conclusion, and checkout step number/name/status/conclusion.
- When `run_attempt>1`, inspect attempt-specific job records if the API exposes them. Otherwise mark attempt-history coverage incomplete; the latest run record is not a complete attempt history.

### Checkout materialization is not Traffic attribution

For each `actions/checkout` step, record the actual job-log inputs and output:

- `checkout_action` (for example, `actions/checkout@v4`)
- `checkout_ref_mode`: `EXPLICIT_MAIN`, `EXPLICIT_SHA`, `DEFAULT_EVENT_REF`, or `UNKNOWN`
- `checkout_ref` when explicit
- `checkout_depth`: numeric `fetch-depth`, when logged
- `checkout_head_sha`: the actual `git log -1 --format=%H` output after checkout
- `run_head_sha`: the Actions run object's event/head SHA
- `head_sha_match`: a comparison of those two independently sourced values, never an assumption

Use two separate classification axes:

1. `checkout_materialization`: `FULL_HISTORY` when `fetch-depth=0`; `SHALLOW_N` when a positive depth N is logged; `UNKNOWN` when not observed. This describes Git history materialized in the runner workspace.
2. `traffic_attribution`: `COUNTED`, `NOT_COUNTED`, or `UNKNOWN`. Only an authorized GitHub Traffic observation can resolve this. Checkout depth, `actions/checkout`, or a run count does not establish a Traffic clone.

When materialization is known but Traffic attribution is not, use the additive classification `CHECKOUT MATERIALIZATION KNOWN / TRAFFIC ATTRIBUTION UNKNOWN`. Keep `traffic_clone_expected` as a planning field, not an observed result. The legacy classification `CONFIRMED NOT A FULL CLONE` must not be interpreted as `checkout_materialization=NONE`; older rows lacking the new fields are UNKNOWN on the materialization axis unless supplemented.

Optional structured fields for new Actions rows: `run_id`, `run_attempt`, `workflow_id`, `job_id`, `step_number`, `step_name`, `checkout_action`, `checkout_ref_mode`, `checkout_ref`, `checkout_depth`, `checkout_materialization`, `run_head_sha`, `checkout_head_sha`, `head_sha_match`, and `traffic_attribution`.

### Append-only supplements and aggregation

- If later job-log evidence resolves checkout depth or SHA for an existing event, append a supplement row with `is_revision=true`, `revision_of=<exact prior event_id>`, `prior_classification`, and `revision_reason`. Do not erase or rewrite the prior event.
- Aggregate checkout events by the unique key `(repository, run_id, run_attempt, job_id, step_number)`. A supplement/revision row is not a second checkout event.

### h853:s3 validation sample

- SAT archive, 2026-11-08 through 2026-11-14: 33 run records on page 1 and 0 on page 2. The 27 previously uninspected runs were examined at job level. Across all 33 runs: 23 checkout jobs and 10 failed FLC test runs with no job records returned. All 33 report `run_attempt=1`.
- The 23 checkout jobs comprise 13 `fetch-depth=0` full-history checkouts and 10 `fetch-depth=2` shallow checkouts. All 23 job logs expose `git log -1 --format=%H`; each checked-out SHA matches the Actions run `head_sha`.
- HsH week and daily run-list queries returned the 2500 cap. Tested hourly buckets were complete: 2026-11-14 23:00-23:59:59Z returned 185 runs (100 + 85 + 0); 13:00-13:59:59Z returned 257 (100 + 100 + 57 + 0). These are method tests, not a completed HsH week census.
- The connector rejected `/traffic/clones?per=day` and `/traffic/views?per=day` as unsupported URL routes. This is a connector-route limitation, not evidence of GitHub permission denial. No Traffic count is claimed.


### Compact Jobs API step-summary omission guard (2026-11-19)

- A compact `actions/runs/{run_id}/jobs` response can return a job record while omitting its step details. An empty or missing `steps` field in that compact response is not evidence that the job had no checkout.
- After job enumeration, use the dedicated workflow-job-steps endpoint and decoded job logs to establish checkout step number/name/status, action, explicit ref, `fetch-depth`, and the actual post-checkout `git log -1 --format=%H` value. Record which source supports each field.
- If the dedicated step endpoint and job log disagree, preserve UNKNOWN and investigate; do not infer a negative checkout observation from a compact summary.
- Counterexample: the two `Maintain H(s)H navigation` jobs #43747347981 and #43747508618 in the 2026-11-15 18:30-18:39:59Z partition had successful step-2 checkouts (`fetch-depth=0`) despite the compact Jobs API summary omitting their step details. The h917:s2 report's four-checkout count is corrected additively; two missing rows were appended, with no prior ledger row rewritten.


## Run-list snapshot retention and job-fan-out gate | 2026-11-19

A completed run-list query is not a durable job-level work queue unless its complete response, or a lossless compact run index, is retained and independently read back before job fan-out.

Required snapshot fields:

- Repository, exact UTC query interval, endpoint and query parameters, per_page, page numbers, returned counts, total_count, terminal-page result, retrieval timestamp, and SHA-256 for each raw page or the complete response.
- For every returned run: run_id, run_attempt, workflow_id, created_at, head_sha, head_branch, event, status, and conclusion.
- Preserve raw page JSON or a lossless ordered index. Verify the stored bytes and digest before treating the enumeration as a recoverable queue.
- Bind every subsequent Jobs API result to its exact run_id and run_attempt. NO_JOB_RECORD_RETURNED is valid only after that exact job endpoint has actually been queried.

If the original response and complete run-ID index are absent, record RUN_ID_SNAPSHOT_NOT_RETAINED, preserve the partition cursor, and recover the source snapshot if possible. Do not silently repeat an already-completed census query. A replacement query requires explicit, documented authorization and must be distinguished from the original enumeration.

Introduction to the Archive

This is primarily a personal archive and indexing system, built so I can access and track my own files more easily. That said, the underlying idea is public: anyone is welcome to consider it, criticize it, share it, fork it, test it, or ignore it.

The project started small. It grew because once the original ontological commitments were established, many later structures seemed to fall into place naturally and intuitively. The archive records that development: the intuitions, the translations, the overextensions, the corrections, the audits, the prediction attempts, and the ongoing effort to separate what is solid from what is speculative.

The archive should be read as a theory-building record, not as a finished theory.

SAT = Scalar–Angular Theory / Scalar–Angular–Torsion Theory

Earlier SAT = Stringing-Along Theory.

The original name was informal and partly self-deprecating. The later names reflect the framework’s central geometric vocabulary: scalar structure, angular interaction, and torsion/twist in four-dimensional worldline geometry.

Core Idea

SAT begins from a simple geometric reversal:

The real physical object is not the point-particle as seen at an instant. The real physical object is the extended four-dimensional worldline.

SAT calls these physicalized worldlines filaments.

A particle, as we observe it, is the intersection between a filament and a moving/resolving time surface.

Fundamental Intuitions of SAT

0th —

  • the real world is the world of particle worldlines plotted in four dimensions
  • this world is a hypercomplex tangled Zottenwelt of worldlines
  • SAT calls these worldlines filaments

1st —

  • time moves like a wavefront through these worldlines
  • SAT calls this wavefront the time surface

2nd —

  • a fundamental particle is the intersection of a filament with the time surface

3rd —

  • there must be a real interaction between the time surface and the filaments
  • this interaction involves energy transfer

4th —

  • filament/time-surface interactions govern particle formation and stability

5th —

  • filament/time-surface interactions exert force back on the time surface

6th —

  • back-transmission from the filament network curves the time surface

7th —

  • filaments and the time surface are physical, not merely conceptual
  • forces may propagate along a filament’s four-dimensional extent
  • “backbleed” effects are structurally self-limiting

8th —

  • known deviations from SM, GR, or QM may be explainable through SAT geometry

9th —

  • particle properties may arise from intersection geometry
  • θ₄ = filament/time-surface interaction angle
  • early SAT treated θ₄ as a primary mass contributor

10th —

  • physical constants should emerge from SAT geometry or phenomena arising from it

Pillars and Propositions

Pillar 1 —

  • the Standard Model describes the evolving three-dimensional structure of matter
  • SAT treats SM structures as importable unless evidence or internal logic forces revision
  • SM behavior is translated into filament/time-surface geometry

Proposition A —

  • the Standard Model is treated as essentially accurate unless forced otherwise

Pillar 2 —

  • the back-pull of the filament structure on the time surface recreates curved spacetime
  • gravity emerges from time-surface curvature induced by filament structure

Proposition B —

  • General Relativity is treated as essentially correct unless forced otherwise

Proposition C —

  • backbleed effects are limited by filament and time-surface geometry
  • causality violations are structurally constrained
  • quantum-scale weirdness may reflect limited cross-slice effects

Pillar 3 —

  • Quantum Mechanics is treated as essentially correct unless forced otherwise
  • QM is translated into the geometry of SAT rather than discarded

Prime General Prediction Pathway —

  • cross-temporal tensions are not explicitly accounted for in SM, GR, or QM
  • this blind spot may produce observable anomalies

Pillar 4 —

  • filament behavior matters, not only filament/time-surface angle
  • vibrating-string, coil, twist, and locking analogies are used as geometric scaffolds
  • particle laws may correspond to repeatable intersection traces
  • QCD-like behavior may arise from two-part and three-part geometric locking

Proposition D —

  • force carriers may be structural transitions rather than persistent filaments
  • light is modeled as an excitation/ripple in the filament network

Proposition E —

  • vacuum and matter may be different regimes of the same filament/time-surface system
  • vacuum may correspond to near-aligned filaments with low energy transfer
  • matter may correspond to higher-misalignment filament intersections

Key Insight —

  • vacuum and matter lie on one continuum of filament/time-surface interaction

Proposition F —

  • some forms of String Theory may be partial mappings of filament/time-surface geometry
  • SAT may import useful string-theoretic structures by translation rather than identity

[L2]   "content": "# Viewing traffic to a repository

Anyone with push access to a repository can view its traffic, including full clones (not fetches), visitors from the past 14 days, referring sites, and popular content in the traffic graph.

You can navigate to referring sites, excluding search engines and GitHub itself, from the links the specific paths were referred from. The popular content links to the specific content that generated traffic.

Referring sites and popular content are ordered by views and unique visitors. Full clones and visitor information update hourly, while referring sites and popular content sections update daily. All data in the traffic graph uses the UTC+0 timezone, regardless of your location.

> \[!TIP]
> You can hover over a specific day in the traffic graph to view the exact data for that day.

![Screenshot showing two line graphs for repository traffic. The lines are marked with dots for specific dates.](/assets/images/help/graphs/repo-traffic-graphs-tooltip-dotcom.png)

## Accessing the traffic graph

1. On GitHub, navigate to the main page of the repository.

2. Under your repository name, click **<svg version="1.1" width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 16 16" class="octicon octicon-graph" aria-label="graph" role="img"><path d="M1.5 1.75V13.5h13.75a.75.75 0 0 1 0 1.5H.75a.75.75 0 0 1-.75-.75V1.75a.75.75 0 0 1 1.5 0Zm14.28 2.53-5.25 5.25a.75.75 0 0 1-1.06 0L7 7.06 4.28 9.78a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042l3.25-3.25a.75.75 0 0 1 1.06 0L10 7.94l4.72-4.72a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042Z"></path></svg> Insights**.

   ![Screenshot of the main page of a repository. In the horizontal navigation bar, a tab, labeled with a graph icon and "Insights," is outlined in orange.](/assets/images/help/repository/repo-nav-insights-tab.png)

3. In the left sidebar, click **Traffic**.

![Screenshot of the "Traffic" tab. The tab is highlighted with a dark orange outline.](/assets/images/help/graphs/traffic-tab.png)",

What Traffic can tell you

GitHub documents these measurements in Viewing traffic to a repository.

1. Views
A view is a visit to a repository page or other GitHub page associated with it.

This can help answer:

How much visible interest is the repository receiving?

Look at:

Total views: overall page traffic
Views by day: whether interest is steady, sporadic, or caused by a specific event
Trend: whether traffic is increasing after a post, conversation, pull request, or publication
But views do not tell you:

whether visitors understood the theory;
whether they agree with it;
whether they read the important files;
whether the same person visited repeatedly.
2. Unique visitors
Unique visitors estimates how many distinct visitors produced those views.

This is usually more informative than total views.

For example:

Pattern	Likely interpretation
100 views / 5 unique visitors	A few people revisiting repeatedly
100 views / 80 unique visitors	Broad but shallow attention
100 views / 90 unique visitors	Many people looked once
100 views / 5 unique visitors, rising daily	A small group may be following the project
The distinction between views and unique visitors is especially important for your repository because you, collaborators, AI tools, or automated processes may revisit it repeatedly.

A clone means someone copied the repository using Git. GitHub’s traffic API describes this as full clones, not ordinary fetches.

Clones can indicate stronger interest than page views because someone may have wanted the files locally. However, a clone still does not prove:

that the person studied the material;
that they ran the code;
that they accepted the theory;
that they were an independent researcher rather than you or an automated process.

Unique cloners
A high clone count with one unique cloner suggests repeated copying by one source. A high number of unique cloners suggests broader distribution.

GitHub’s official API documentation describes the clone measurements in REST API endpoints for repository traffic.

Google or another search engine

a personal website
another GitHub repository
a direct link from a conversation or social platform
This is useful for answering:

How are people discovering the archive?

Interpretation examples:

GitHub as the main referrer: people are finding it through GitHub navigation, profiles, links, or related repositories.
Search engines: the archive is being discovered through public web search.
A social site: a specific post or discussion may be driving attention.
No meaningful referrers: people may be arriving directly through bookmarks, copied links, or private conversations.
GitHub excludes some sources, including GitHub itself and search engines, from certain referral displays; the official documentation explains the limitations.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      - "indexes/STRUCTURAL_INDEX.md"
      - "indexes/index-state.json"
      - "indexes/CONVERSATION_CHRONOLOGY.md"
      - "indexes/LIVE_CONVERSATION_CHRONOLOGY.md"
      - "indexes/manifests/**"
      - "indexes/autotag/**"
      - "CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json"
      - "CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/curated/**"

permissions:
  contents: write
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: hsh-navigation-main
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  maintain:
    if: ${{ github.event_name != 'push' || !contains(github.event.head_commit.message, '[skip hsh-maintenance]') }}
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45

    steps:
      - name: Check out current main branch
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Date-tag stable developmental exports
        id: development_dates
        continue-on-error: true
        run: |
          mkdir -p indexes/manifests
          if [ -d "DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS" ]; then
            python tools/date_conversation_exports.py \
              "DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS" \
              --apply \
              --resolve-collisions \
              --manifest indexes/manifests/development-conversation-dates.json
          else
            echo "DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS not present; skipping"
          fi

      - name: Date-tag LIVE CONVOS preserving original source content
        id: live_dates
        continue-on-error: true
        run: |
          mkdir -p indexes/manifests
          if [ -d "LIVE CONVOS" ]; then
            python tools/date_conversation_exports.py \
              "LIVE CONVOS" \
              --apply \
              --resolve-collisions \
              --manifest indexes/manifests/live-conversation-dates.json
          else
            echo "LIVE CONVOS not present; skipping"
          fi

      - name: Date-tag repository-root and other conversation exports
        id: root_dates
        continue-on-error: true
        run: |
          python tools/date_conversation_exports.py "." --apply --resolve-collisions --manifest indexes/manifests/root-conversation-dates.json

      - name: Verify every datable source now has the right filename date prefix
        run: python tools/audit_conversation_date_tags.py --output indexes/manifests/date-tag-audit.json --strict

      - name: Build conversation viewer from the fresh manifests
        run: python tools/build_conversation_viewer_resolved.py

      - name: Build conversation chronology indexes
        run: |
          if [ -d "DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS" ]; then
            python tools/index_conversation_chronology.py \
              "DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS" \
              --output indexes/CONVERSATION_CHRONOLOGY.md
          fi
          if [ -d "LIVE CONVOS" ]; then
            python tools/index_conversation_chronology.py \
              "LIVE CONVOS" \
              --output indexes/LIVE_CONVERSATION_CHRONOLOGY.md
          fi
          python tools/index_conversation_chronology.py "." --output indexes/OTHER_HSH_CONVERSATION_CHRONOLOGY.md

      - name: Refresh repository structural index before tag cross-check
        run: python tools/index_archive.py --root .

      - name: Build archive-wide conversation autotag indexes
        run: |
          mkdir -p WORKSPACES/COMMON/analysis indexes/autotag
          python WORKSPACES/COMMON/scripts/layered_autotag_nathan_v3.py . \
            --out WORKSPACES/COMMON/analysis/archive_layered_autotags.jsonl \
            --summary indexes/autotag/AUTOTAG_SUMMARY.md \
            --index indexes/autotag/CONVERSATION_TAG_INDEX.md \
            --manifest indexes/autotag/conversation-tag-manifest.json \
            --user-tag-index indexes/autotag/user-message-tags.jsonl \
            --structural-index-state indexes/index-state.json \
            --window 4

      - name: Refresh structural index with autotag surfaces included
        run: python tools/index_archive.py --root .

      - name: Validate Python tooling
        run: |
          python -m py_compile WORKSPACES/COMMON/scripts/layered_autotag_nathan.py
          python -m py_compile WORKSPACES/COMMON/scripts/layered_autotag_nathan_v2.py
          python -m py_compile WORKSPACES/COMMON/scripts/layered_autotag_nathan_v3.py

      - name: Validate viewer JavaScript
        run: |
          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/annotations.js
          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/viewer.js
          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/argus_followup.js
          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/provenance_search.js
          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/landmarks.js
          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/presentation.js

      - name: Run repository tests
        run: python -m unittest discover -s tests -v

      - name: Validate generated navigation state
        run: |
          python -m json.tool indexes/index-state.json >/dev/null
          if [ -f indexes/manifests/development-conversation-dates.json ]; then
            python -m json.tool indexes/manifests/development-conversation-dates.json >/dev/null
          fi
          if [ -f indexes/manifests/live-conversation-dates.json ]; then
            python -m json.tool indexes/manifests/live-conversation-dates.json >/dev/null
          fi
          python -m json.tool indexes/autotag/conversation-tag-manifest.json >/dev/null
          test -s indexes/autotag/CONVERSATION_TAG_INDEX.md
          test -s indexes/autotag/user-message-tags.jsonl
          python -m json.tool CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json >/dev/null
          python - <<'PY'
          import json
          from pathlib import Path

          data = json.loads(Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          missing = [
              item['path']
              for item in data['conversations']
              if not item.get('external') and not Path(item['path']).is_file()
          ]
          assert not missing, f'viewer catalog contains missing repository source paths: {missing}'
          PY
          test -f indexes/STRUCTURAL_INDEX.md
          test -f indexes/CONVERSATION_CHRONOLOGY.md || true

      - name: Report date-tagging warnings
        if: ${{ steps.development_dates.outcome == 'failure' || steps.live_dates.outcome == 'failure' }}
        run: |
          echo "::warning::At least one date-tagging pass reported a collision or parse-level failure. Generated manifests were retained; structural/chronology indexing continued."

      - name: Commit maintained navigation, tag indexes, and viewer artifacts
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config user.name "H(s)H Navigation Bot"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add -A -- "DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS" "LIVE CONVOS" || true
          git add -A -- '*.json' '*.txt' || true
          git add indexes/STRUCTURAL_INDEX.md indexes/index-state.json || true
          git add indexes/CONVERSATION_CHRONOLOGY.md indexes/LIVE_CONVERSATION_CHRONOLOGY.md indexes/OTHER_HSH_CONVERSATION_CHRONOLOGY.md || true
          git add indexes/manifests indexes/autotag || true
          git add -A CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/curated || true
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
            echo "Navigation, tag indexes, and viewer data already current"
          else
            git commit -m "[skip hsh-maintenance] Maintain date/index/tag/viewer navigation"
            if ! git push origin HEAD:main; then
              echo "::error::Main advanced while this run was working. Because this workflow can rename source conversation files as well as regenerate indexes, it will not merge or replay a stale snapshot. A fresh maintenance run must recompute from current main."
              exit 1
            fi
          fi

      - name: Upload full message-level autotag analysis
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: archive-wide-layered-autotags
          path: WORKSPACES/COMMON/analysis/archive_layered_autotags.jsonl

      - name: Configure GitHub Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v5

      - name: Upload current conversation viewer
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: CONVERSATION_VIEWER

      - name: Deploy current conversation viewer
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
",
